The underline offset and thickness are in em, so they scale with the text, and the focus ring is drawn again on every line when a link wraps. external opens a new tab with rel=noopener, adds a small up-right arrow that stays on the last word and a hidden 'opens in a new tab'. download is true, a file name, or { filename, type, size }: type and size ({ type: 'PDF', size: 2_411_000 }) are shown as 'PDF, 2.4 MB', with the size written out in the locale you pass, and a screen reader hears 'download' before them. current marks the link to the page you are on with aria-current (page by default, or 'step', 'location', 'date', 'time') and a heavier weight. disabled renders a span with role=link and aria-disabled instead of an anchor, so it is never a dead tab stop. hrefLang sets the attribute and adds a hidden 'in German' (the name comes from Intl.DisplayNames). asChild puts the same look on your framework link: pass <Link href> with the text inside as the only child. labels holds the hidden words for another language. textLinkVariants is exported so other components can borrow the look.

items.name: text-link-demo
items.title: Text link demo
items.description: A working preview of Text link.

items.name: count-tabs
items.title: Count tabs
items.description: Tabs with a count by every label (Open 12, Closed 48): tabular figures, 99+ above a limit, a skeleton while loading, read out as 'Open, 12 items'.
items.docs: tabs is a list of { value, label, count, loading, disabled }. Control the selected tab with value and onValueChange, or leave them out and use defaultValue (the first tab by default); the panels are TabsContent from @rhs-ui/primitives/tabs, passed as children, or leave them out and show one list yourself. variant is line (an underline) or pill (a segmented control). Counts are written in tabular figures in the locale you pass and collapse to '99+' above max (99 by default). The accessible name of a tab is its label and its count, 'Open, 12 items' ('Open, 1 item', 'Shipped, more than 99 items'), so the number is read out with the tab; labels holds those words for another language. loading puts a small skeleton where the number goes and the name says 'loading count'. A tab with a count of zero dims but is not disabled, so the empty view stays reachable (use disabled to switch one off). Arrow keys, Home and End move and select, as in Tabs. When the count of the selected tab changes, one polite announcement says so ('Open, 13 items'); a count that changes in another tab, and the first render, say nothing. A row that is wider than its box scrolls sideways, with room inside the scroller for the focus ring. Without children there are no panels, so the tabs carry no aria-controls.

items.name: count-tabs-demo
items.title: Count tabs demo
items.description: A working preview of Count tabs.

items.name: cursor-pagination
items.title: Cursor pagination
items.description: Older and Newer for feeds and APIs that page by cursor: no page numbers, no total, a spinner that keeps the button's width and a plain end state.
items.docs: Pass hasPrevious and hasNext from your API (a cursor, a next-page token, a Link header) and handle onPrevious and onNext; previous is the newer page and next the older one. loading is 'previous', 'next' or false and says which way a request is in flight: that button shows a spinner in place of its arrow, so it keeps its width, and is marked aria-busy, while the other one waits, dimmed. Neither is disabled, so a keyboard user keeps their place and a second press does nothing. When there is nothing further the button is replaced by plain text, 'No newer results' at the start of the list and 'No older results' at the end, instead of a dead control. range is your own text ('21 to 40') in a polite live region, so a screen reader hears where it landed after each step; at an end of the list the same region also says so ('16 to 20. No older results.'). The range is empty until you give it one. When the button that was used with the keyboard (or a click that focused it) is replaced by its end text, focus moves onto the text, so a keyboard user is not thrown out of the list; if the reader has moved on by then, focus is left alone. hrefs ({ previous, next }) makes the buttons real links, for pages a crawler can follow and a reader can open in a new tab; with a handler as well, a plain click goes to the handler and a middle or modified click opens the address. With links and no handlers it can be rendered from a Server Component (a page.tsx): the component is a client component, so only data goes in, and the links are in the HTML. labels holds the four texts for another language. In a container narrower than 24rem the range moves above the two buttons.

items.name: cursor-pagination-demo
items.title: Cursor pagination demo
items.description: A working preview of Cursor pagination.

items.name: dot-stepper
items.title: Dot stepper
items.description: Page dots for onboarding, carousels and short flows: the current dot stretches into a pill, each dot can be a button, and past seven a window slides.
items.docs: count is how many steps there are and value the current one, counted from 0. Give it onValueChange and every dot becomes a button inside a list (label names the list, 'Steps' by default); each button is named 'Step 3 of 5' and, with labels (one name per dot: ['Welcome', 'Invite your team', ...]), 'Step 2 of 5, Invite your team'; the current one is marked aria-current='step'. Without onValueChange the dots are one picture with a single name, 'Step 2 of 5' (format changes the words; {current} and {total} are the numbers, and a label is added for the current step). The current dot stretches into a pill and the others stay small. Past seven dots the row no longer grows: a window of five slides along as value moves, the dots at its edges shrink to say there is more, and the dots outside the window are hidden and cannot be tabbed to; each button still knows its place in the whole (aria-posinset and aria-setsize). size is sm, md or lg and orientation horizontal or vertical. The dots, and the focus ring, are drawn in currentColor, so a dark photo takes text-white and shows a white ring. As buttons the dots sit 24px apart, so each button is a 24 by 24px target (WCAG 2.5.8); as a picture they sit closer. A dot that is not current is half strength, and the focus ring has room inside the clip. The stretch and the slide are instant under reduced motion. It keeps no state of its own: it is a view of value.

items.name: dot-stepper-demo
items.title: Dot stepper demo
items.description: A working preview of Dot stepper.

items.name: compact-stepper
items.title: Compact stepper
items.description: A stepper for small spaces: 'Step 2 of 5, Shipping' over a segmented bar, with the full list of steps and their states one tap away.
items.docs: steps is the list of { id, label, description, state, href } and current the index of the step in progress, counted from 0. A step before current is done and one after it is upcoming; set state to 'error' on a step that needs attention. The top line is the counter and the name of the current step ('Step 2 of 5', 'Shipping') in one polite live region, so moving on is announced once; a current step in error also says 'Needs attention' beside its name. Under it a segmented bar has one segment per step: done is a mid grey, the current one is solid and upcoming ones are faint, and the bar is hidden from assistive technology because the text already says it. The All steps button opens a popover, a dialog named 'All steps', with every step, its description and its state in words (Done, Current, Needs attention); the state word sits beside the name and the description has the full width of the row under it. With allowJumpBack, done steps and steps in error before the current one become links in that list when they have an href or you give onStepSelect (a button, or an anchor when the step has an href), and choosing one calls onStepSelect(id, index) and closes the list; upcoming steps and the current one are always plain text. A stepper that is read-only, or whose steps have an href and no onStepSelect, can be rendered from a Server Component; onStepSelect is a function and needs a client parent. A step in error that is not the current one is also named under the bar ('Payment needs attention'). size is md or sm, and labels holds every word for another language. It works in any width, from a 240px column to a full-width header.

items.name: compact-stepper-demo
items.title: Compact stepper demo
items.description: A working preview of Compact stepper.

items.name: adaptive-pagination
items.title: Adaptive pagination
items.description: One pagination that fits its box: numbered pages when there is room, 'Page 3 of 12' with a list of pages and arrows when there is not.
items.docs: page is the current page counted from 1 and pageCount how many there are; onPageChange(page) is called with the page asked for. It measures the width of its own container with a ResizeObserver, never the window, so one component fits a narrow card and a wide table footer. When the container is wide enough it shows first, previous, a window of page numbers with ellipses (siblingCount numbers on each side of the current page, 1 by default, always the same number of slots so the row does not jump), next and last. When it is not, it shows previous, a button that reads 'Page 3 of 12' and opens a grid of every page in a dialog named by its heading, 'Go to page' (arrow keys, Home, End and the Page keys move, it opens on the current page), and next. Until it has been measured the compact layout stands in, because it fits anywhere. The current page carries aria-current='page'. The buttons that go back on the first page and the ones that go on at the last are aria-disabled rather than disabled: they keep focus and a tooltip says why ('You are on the first page'). A change of layout never loses the focused control: previous and next are the same elements in both layouts, and a page number, first or last hands focus to the compact label, previous or next (and the label back to the current page number). hrefFor(page) returns an address and turns every control into a real link for crawlers and new tabs; from a Server Component, which cannot pass a function, give hrefTemplate such as '/orders?page={page}'. With a handler too, a plain click goes to onPageChange and a modified click opens the address. The change is announced politely as 'Page 4 of 12'. align places the row (center by default), locale writes the numbers, and labels holds every word for another language.

items.name: adaptive-pagination-demo
items.title: Adaptive pagination demo
items.description: A working preview of Adaptive pagination.

items.name: breadcrumb-siblings
items.title: Breadcrumb with siblings
items.description: A breadcrumb where each level opens a menu of its siblings, so people move sideways without going up first. Long trails fold, long lists filter.
items.docs: items is the trail from the top to the page you are on: { label, href, siblings }. The last item is the current page and is not a link. A crumb with siblings, a list of { label, href } for the pages at its level (itself included), gets a small chevron beside its label: the label stays a link to the crumb's own page and the chevron is a separate button named 'Pages in Projects' ('Pages in {label}'), so both actions work from the keyboard. The menu checks the entry whose href is the crumb's own (aria-current is 'location' for a level above and 'page' for the last crumb), and a list of twelve or fewer opens as a menu. A longer list opens as a dialog instead, named 'Pages in Projects', because a menu may hold only items and not a field: the filter field is in focus, typing filters, Enter follows the first match, Arrow Down moves into the links and Arrow Up from the first one returns to the field, Escape closes, the number of matches is said politely ('5 of 18 pages') and a filter that matches nothing says so. onNavigate(href) takes a plain click on a crumb or a sibling, for a client router; without it the links are followed, and a modified click always opens the address. maxVisible (default 4) is the most crumbs shown: a longer trail keeps the first crumb and the last maxVisible minus one, and the levels in between fold into a menu behind a '...' button right after the first crumb (named 'Show 2 more levels', or 'Show 1 more level'). separator is a slash by default and can be any node. It is built on Breadcrumb, so the nav landmark, the ordered list, the hidden separators and aria-current are the same as the plain one; labels holds the words for another language. The trail stays on one line and measures itself: when it does not fit its box, more levels fold into the same menu, one at a time starting next to the first crumb, until the label of the current page is whole (the first crumb and the current page always stay), and they come back when the box grows. Short of that only the label of the current page gives way, with an ellipsis; the other crumbs keep their labels, up to a maximum width, and the gaps tighten on a phone.

items.name: breadcrumb-siblings-demo
items.title: Breadcrumb with siblings demo
items.description: A working preview of Breadcrumb with siblings.

items.name: nav-rail
items.title: Nav rail
items.description: A slim vertical rail of icon destinations with tooltips, badges, a top slot and a pinned bottom group, for apps with many areas.
items.docs: items is the list of areas: { id, label, icon, href, badge, badgeLabel, group }. icon is an element (<IconHome />), label is the tooltip, the label under the icon and the accessible name, and an area with an href is a link while one without is a button. current is the id of the area you are in: it is filled and marked aria-current='page'. onSelect(id) is called when one is chosen; on an area with an href a plain click goes to it and a modified click opens the address. badge is a number (the NotificationBadge count: hidden at 0, '99+' above 99) or true for a dot, and badgeLabel (default 'updates') says what it stands for, so a screen reader hears 'Messages 3 unread messages' for a count and 'Reports New report' for a dot: the label comes first in the markup and is drawn after the icon. Entries that follow each other with the same group sit together, and a thin rule is drawn where the group changes. top holds the brand mark; bottom is pinned under the list, for settings and the account, and NavRailItem (label, icon, href, current, onSelect) makes entries there that match the rest. The list is a plain ul inside a nav landmark (label, 'Main' by default), so Tab walks it. On a short screen the list scrolls on its own and top and bottom stay in place, with room inside the scroller for the focus ring. showLabels widens the rail and puts each name under its icon, so the tooltips are not needed. expandOnHover keeps the rail's width and slides a labelled panel over the content when the pointer is over it or focus is inside it, so nothing shifts; expanded holds that panel open. Reduced motion shows it without the slide.

items.name: nav-rail-demo
items.title: Nav rail demo
items.description: A working preview of Nav rail.

items.name: top-bar
items.title: Top bar
items.description: The app bar of a phone-first screen: a back button, a title that truncates properly, trailing actions and a large title that settles on scroll.
items.docs: Put the bar inside the element that scrolls, as its first child: with sticky (the default) it stays at the top, and the nearest scrolling parent is found by itself (scrollContainer takes a ref when it is another element). title is the name of the screen and subtitle a lighter line under it. onBack shows a back button, a chevron named by backLabel ('Back to orders'; 'Back' by default), and backHref makes it a link that onBack still handles on a plain click; leading replaces it with your own element. actions is a list of { id, label, icon, onSelect, href, disabled, destructive, priority, pinned } shown as icon buttons named by their label. The bar measures itself: when the back button, the whole title and the actions no longer fit, the actions fold into a 'More actions' menu before the title is cut, the lowest priority first (equal priorities from the end), pinned ones never; only when even the menu button leaves too little room does the title truncate with an ellipsis, and its full text stays in the page for assistive technology. large adds a big title under the bar that scrolls away with the content; as it goes under the bar the bar's own title fades in, the progress being read from where the big title is, not from a number you pass. The title is always the one heading: the large one when there is one (the bar's copy is then hidden from assistive technology) and the bar's own otherwise, so the outline never doubles; as sets its level, h1 by default, so pass h2 or lower on a page that has its own h1. The bar adds the top safe-area inset (env(safe-area-inset-top), or the CSS variable --top-bar-inset when that is larger, for a frame that draws its own notch). A sticky bar has a bottom border only once content has scrolled under it (once the large title has gone, when there is one); a bar that is not sticky always has one; borderless removes it. labels holds the two hidden names for another language.

items.name: top-bar-demo
items.title: Top bar demo
items.description: A working preview of Top bar.

items.name: floating-player
items.title: Floating player
items.description: Keeps a playing video in view: when it scrolls away it docks to a corner as a mini player that never restarts, with a close button.
items.docs: Wrap any player in it (a video element, an iframe or your own component) and tell it whether the media is playing with playing. While the player is on screen nothing changes. When it scrolls out of view during playback, the same element docks to a corner as a mini player (dock is bottom-right by default or bottom-left, width is a number of px or any CSS length, 320 by default, never wider than the screen minus 2rem): the child is not moved or re-created, only restyled with position fixed, so playback never restarts, and a placeholder of the same height, with a dashed outline and a short note, keeps the page from jumping and shows where it went. It counts as in view while about a fifth of it is on screen. A video that is not playing is never docked; once docked, pausing keeps the mini player so it can be resumed. The mini player is a labelled region ('Product tour, mini player', from label) with a Close button and a 'Back to video' link that scrolls to the placeholder; Escape closes it from inside it and from anywhere nothing else has focus (a menu or dialog that takes the key keeps it), and docking is announced once. Closing calls onClose, where you pause the media, and the player stays in its place until the video has been seen again; onDock(true | false) tells you when it docks and when it returns. Focus goes to the player when the mini player closes or you go back. It keeps clear of a phone's safe area (env(safe-area-inset-*), at least 1rem from each edge), and under reduced motion it docks without the slide. Do not put it inside an element with a transform, filter or contain: paint, which would make fixed mean fixed inside that element. The scroll can be the page's or any scroll container's. labels holds the words for another language. The rhs-float-in keyframes and its animate-rhs-float-in variable come with the item.

items.name: floating-player-demo
items.title: Floating player demo
items.description: A working preview of Floating player.

items.name: alphabet-index
items.title: Alphabet index
items.description: An A to Z rail to jump through a long list: drag a finger down it, see the letter in a bubble, skip the empty letters.
items.docs: Put it beside a scrolling list and give it a height (h-full inside a flex row). Pass letters as a string or an array (years and numbers work), available for the letters that have entries, value for the one your list is showing, and scroll the list to that section in onSelect. Press or drag along the rail with a finger, a pen or a mouse: onSelect is called once per letter crossed, the bubble shows it, and letters without entries give way to the nearest one that has some. For the keyboard it is a list of buttons: Tab enters it at the current letter, the arrow keys, Home and End move, Enter selects, and Tab or Shift+Tab leaves it from wherever focus is. Set bubble to false to leave the bubble out.

items.name: alphabet-index-demo
items.title: Alphabet index demo
items.description: A working preview of Alphabet index.

items.name: route-focus
items.title: Route focus
items.description: After a client-side navigation it moves focus to the new page's heading and announces the title once, as the browser does for full loads.
items.docs: Mount it once in the root layout and pass the pathname from your router (usePathname() in Next.js). When the path changes it moves focus to the page's main heading, or to the element you name with target (a selector or a ref), and says the page title once in a polite live region. The first render, a change of hash or query string, and a navigation while the person is typing in a field do nothing to focus. The target gets a temporary tabindex of -1 and shows no outline unless focus arrived by keyboard. Pass resetScroll if your router does not scroll to the top by itself.

items.name: route-focus-demo
items.title: Route focus demo
items.description: A working preview of Route focus.

items.name: stage-path
items.title: Stage path
items.description: A chevron path through stages (Lead, Qualified, Proposal, Won): done, current and next, clickable when you allow it.
items.docs: Pass stages (id, label, optional date and note) and current, the id of the stage the item is at. Without onStageChange it is a read-only record. With it, every stage you may go to is a button that calls onStageChange(id, from) before anything moves: change current yourself when you accept, and return a promise to have the stage shown as busy meanwhile. Going back to a finished stage needs allowBackward. lostLabel adds a terminal outcome (it calls onStageChange with the id "lost"), and lost draws the item as ended there, with current as the last stage it reached. When a press made with the keyboard or a pointer moves the item, focus follows it to the stage it is at (or the outcome), which is no longer a button, so the keyboard keeps its place; the arrow keys pass through that stage and Tab still goes from button to button. A screen reader hears an ordered list (Stage 3 of 5: Proposal, current) and, politely, what happened (Proposal, stage 3 of 5, or Closed lost at stage 3 of 5; every sentence can be reworded through labels); in a box under 28rem only the current stage keeps its name and the others shrink to a check or a number.

items.name: stage-path-demo
items.title: Stage path demo
items.description: A working preview of Stage path.

items.name: category-strip
items.title: Category strip
items.description: A scrolling row of icon-and-label categories with the current one underlined, for browsing marketplaces and stays.
items.docs: Pass categories (id, label, icon, href, count) and current. Without an href an item is a button marked aria-pressed and onSelect(id) is called; with one it is a link marked aria-current="page", drawn by linkAs (your router Link), and onSelect, if given, takes the plain click over so you can route yourself. The row scrolls sideways behind fade edges with arrows that appear only where more is hidden, a mouse can drag it and it glides on, touch keeps its momentum, and the arrow keys, Home and End move between the items with one tab stop for the whole strip. When the row first appears with the current category inside a fade, it is centred (and kept centred while a web font widens the labels, until you scroll, press a key or focus an item), and it scrolls into view when it changes. Labels are never cut: a label sets the width of its item. size is sm, md or lg. Without panels: choosing a category only changes what your page shows below.

items.name: category-strip-demo
items.title: Category strip demo
items.description: A working preview of Category strip.

items.name: lazy-tabs
items.title: Lazy tabs
items.description: Tabs whose panels load when first opened, with a skeleton, an error and Retry per panel, and the loaded ones kept.
items.docs: Give each tab a load: a function that returns a promise of the panel content, run the first time the tab opens, or plain content for a tab that needs no request. A panel shows the skeleton you pass (per tab or for all), then the content, which is kept so coming back is instant. If the promise rejects the panel says Could not load <tab> with a Retry button (an Error message is shown under it), and no other panel is touched. prefetchOnHover starts a tab after the pointer rests on it for a moment, or at once on focus. A loading tab swaps its icon for a spinner in the same box (a tab without an icon pulses its label), so no tab ever moves while another loads, and its panel is aria-busy; a request is never cancelled by leaving the tab. A row wider than its box scrolls sideways behind fade edges with the selected tab kept in view. keepMounted keeps loaded panels mounted (hidden) so their state survives. Panels are drawn from tabs, so there are no TabsContent children.

items.name: lazy-tabs-demo
items.title: Lazy tabs demo
items.description: A working preview of Lazy tabs.

items.name: closable-tabs
items.title: Closable tabs
items.description: Tabs you can close and add: a close button on each tab, a plus at the end, and a sensible tab chosen after closing.
items.docs: Pass tabs (id, label, icon, closable, dirty), value and onValueChange, and render TabsContent panels as children. Each tab has a close button named Close <label>; a middle click or Delete on a tab asks for it to close as well. onClose(id) is only a request: nothing closes until you remove the tab from tabs, so you can show a confirmation first. When the selected tab goes, the nearest neighbour (to its right, else to its left) is selected through onValueChange and takes focus. A dirty tab shows a dot instead of the close button until hover or focus and says unsaved changes in its name. onAdd adds the plus button; at maxTabs it stays focusable, dimmed, and explains why. A tab with closable false is pinned: it has no close button, and a small pin stands where the button would be so every tab keeps the same room. Overflow scrolls behind fade edges with the selected tab kept in view; the arrows appear where there is a hover, and touch swipes. If you confirm in a dialog, focus is put on the neighbour tab after the dialog has closed; when the person keeps the tab, return focus to it in the dialog's onCloseAutoFocus.

items.name: closable-tabs-demo
items.title: Closable tabs demo
items.description: A working preview of Closable tabs.

items.name: archive-nav
items.title: Archive nav
items.description: A blog or changelog archive by year and month, with post counts, the current period open and the rest folded.
items.docs: Pass periods (year and months, each with month 1 to 12, count and href), current ({ year, month }) and your application locale. The current year is open and the others are disclosure buttons with aria-expanded; a month is a link (drawn by linkAs, your router Link) only if it has posts, and the current one is marked aria-current="page". Without an href, a month is a button that calls onNavigate. Month names are worked out from the locale. The newest collapsedCount years (default 5) show and the rest sit behind a Show earlier years button that never moves, so keyboard focus stays on it; if the current page is in an older year they start shown. The list is one nav landmark, named Archive by default.

items.name: archive-nav-demo
items.title: Archive nav demo
items.description: A working preview of Archive nav.

items.name: load-earlier
items.title: Load earlier
items.description: Load earlier messages at the top of a feed without the scroll jumping: it keeps your place when older items arrive.
items.docs: Put it first in the scrolling list, above the items, and pass hasEarlier, loading, error and onLoadEarlier. When the older items are added above, the row keeps the reader on the item they were looking at: it measures that item before and after and corrects the scroll position by the difference, so it works where the browser does not anchor the scroll and does not correct twice where it does. Pass scrollRef when the list scrolls inside a box (otherwise the nearest scrolling ancestor, or the page, is used). Set auto to load when the row scrolls into view; the button stays as the fallback. Pass count and noun to have what arrived announced once as a count (12 earlier messages loaded). Keep the list itself out of a live region, or every old message would be read out. The row has four states: the button, a spinner row, an error with Retry, and a quiet start of the conversation.

items.name: load-earlier-demo
items.title: Load earlier demo
items.description: A working preview of Load earlier.

items.name: accessible-feed
items.title: Accessible feed
items.description: An infinite feed built to the WAI-ARIA feed pattern: each article is a stop, and Page Down and Page Up move between them.
items.docs: Pass items, renderItem (what is inside an article), labelFor (the name of an article), hasMore, loading and onLoadMore. The container is role=feed and aria-busy while loading; every item is an article and a tab stop with aria-posinset, aria-setsize (-1 while the total is unknown, or the total you pass) and aria-label. Page Down and Page Up move focus to the next and previous article; Page Down on the last one asks for more and moves on when it arrives; Ctrl+End and Ctrl+Home leave the feed for the next or previous focusable element. New items never take focus. Under the feed it renders InfiniteScrollStatus: loading by itself near the viewport, a visible Load more button, an error with Retry and the end; pass status for its words, noun and margin. articleClassName styles each article; the look inside is yours.

items.name: accessible-feed-demo
items.title: Accessible feed demo
items.description: A working preview of Accessible feed.

items.name: swipe-tabs
items.title: Swipe tabs
items.description: Tabs for phones: panels swipe sideways on scroll-snap, the underline follows your finger between tabs, and a mouse gets plain tabs with arrow keys.
items.docs: Give it a height when the panels should scroll on their own (h-full inside a flex column, or a fixed height); without one it is as tall as its tallest panel. Pass tabs (value, label, icon, content), then value and onValueChange to control it, or defaultValue. The panels are one row of scroll-snap, so the browser does the swiping and the momentum: a swipe selects the new tab once the track has settled, a tap on a tab slides to its panel, and the underline and the label colours are drawn from the scroll position on every frame. Only the selected panel is exposed to assistive technology; the others are inert. lazy mounts the selected panel and its neighbours only, and a tap on a far tab starts one panel away so the slide never shows a blank. swipeable={false} leaves the tabs and the arrow keys (Left, Right, Home, End) as the only way to move. Under reduced motion the slide is an instant change. A bar of tabs wider than the screen scrolls with the underline, keeps the selected tab in view and fades at the edge it continues past. It follows right-to-left text. A controlled parent that refuses a change gets the track slid back to the selected tab. Use barClassName for a sticky bar and panelClassName for the padding of the panels.

items.name: swipe-tabs-demo
items.title: Swipe tabs demo
items.description: A working preview of Swipe tabs.

items.name: floating-tab-bar
items.title: Floating tab bar
items.description: A floating, pill-shaped tab bar for mobile web: only the current tab shows its label, five fit in 320px, and it clears the home indicator.
items.docs: Pass items (id, label, icon, href, badge), current and onSelect. Only the current item shows its label, with an animated width that is instant under reduced motion; the other items are icons that keep their label as the accessible name, so three to five destinations fit on a phone. badge is a count or true for a dot, from NotificationBadge. The bar is fixed to the bottom and pads for the safe area (the page needs viewport-fit=cover in its viewport meta for the inset to have a value); to pin it inside a frame instead, pass className="absolute" to a positioned parent. hideOnScroll slides it away while the page scrolls down and brings it back on any upward move, at the top of the page, and when a key brings focus into it; scrollRef names an element that scrolls instead of the page, and it must exist before the bar. With linkAs it renders in a Server Component (only the scroll behaviour is client code); onSelect is a function, so use it from a Client Component.

items.name: floating-tab-bar-demo
items.title: Floating tab bar demo
items.description: A working preview of Floating tab bar.

items.name: expanding-search
items.title: Expanding search
items.description: A header search icon that grows into a field in place, with suggestions, Escape to fold back and a full-bar cover on phones.
items.docs: Put it in the end of a header; the header should be position: relative, because on a phone the field covers it. Control the text with value and onValueChange (or defaultValue), handle Enter with onSubmit, and pass suggestions (strings or { value, hint }) that you have filtered yourself: they appear under the field while it has focus, with arrow keys, Enter and the typed part in bold, and a click on a row calls onSubmit with it. expandedWidth sets how wide the field grows on a screen wider than a phone (a number of px or a CSS length), align="start" grows it towards the end instead. listOpen shows the suggestions whatever has focus, for a preview or your own logic. shortcut opens it from anywhere outside other fields: "/" or "mod+k". Escape and the close button fold it back and return focus to the icon; leaving an empty field folds it too, and one with text stays open so a query is never thrown away. A folded field keeps its text and shows a dot on the icon. The button is named Search and reports aria-expanded. Pass open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange to control it, and autoFocus to focus a field that mounts open.

items.name: expanding-search-demo
items.title: Expanding search demo
items.description: A working preview of Expanding search.

items.name: toc-rail
items.title: Contents rail
items.description: A quiet contents rail for long articles: one mark per heading in the page gutter, opening into the titles on hover, focus or a touch button.
items.docs: Put it in a column of the page next to the article, in the outer gutter, and leave about 16rem free there: the rail is 2.5rem wide at rest and grows over the gutter, never over the text. Pass items (id, title, level 1 to 3) in page order; the ids are the ids of the headings. It follows the scroll by itself, or takes activeId. offset is the room, in px, a fixed header takes: the rail sticks that far from the top and a heading counts as reached when it passes that line (give the headings scroll-margin-top to match). side="left" mirrors it. It is a nav with a list of links and aria-current="location": a mouse opens it by pointing, the keyboard by Tab, and a small button, drawn only where the pointer is a finger, holds it open (open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange). Below the lg breakpoint it is hidden: put a contents control at the top of the article for phones.

items.name: toc-rail-demo
items.title: Contents rail demo
items.description: A working preview of Contents rail.

items.name: story-progress
items.title: Story progress
items.description: Segmented progress bars for stories and slideshows: tap the thirds to move, hold to pause, nothing advances under reduced motion.
items.docs: It wraps the media area: pass count, the slide you are on as index with onIndexChange (or defaultIndex), and put the current slide in children, leaving about 3rem free at the top for the segments and the buttons. duration is a number of ms or one per slide; onComplete is called when the last slide's time is up and when someone goes forward from it; going back from the first slide restarts it. A press on the left third goes back and on the right third goes on; holding anywhere pauses while it is down. Links, buttons and fields inside the slide keep working. Keyboard users get Left and Right on the story, a Pause button, and Previous and Next buttons that appear on focus; "Slide 2 of 5" is said once in a polite live region. paused and onPausedChange control the Pause button, autoplay={false} stops the timer so the current segment is simply full, and a hidden tab pauses by itself. The fill is a CSS animation, so pausing keeps the exact place, and under reduced motion nothing advances on its own and the Pause button is not drawn. tone="media" draws white segments for a photo or a dark slide; actions adds buttons beside Pause.

items.name: story-progress-demo
items.title: Story progress demo
items.description: A working preview of Story progress.

items.name: card-tabs
items.title: Card tabs
items.description: Tabs whose triggers are cards with an icon, a title and a line, for choosing between jobs, plans or modes, with real tabpanels and 2D arrow keys.
items.docs: Pass tabs (value, title, description, icon, count, disabled), value and onValueChange (or defaultValue), and CardTabsContent panels as children, one per value. orientation="horizontal" is a grid of columns cards per row from the sm breakpoint (default the number of tabs, at most 3) and a single column on a phone; "vertical" is a list beside the panel from md up. The selected card has a stronger border and an inverted icon tile, which read without colour. They are real tabs, and a card is named by what it shows (title, count and line), so what someone sees is what a voice command or a screen reader says; arrow keys move and select, and Up and Down also move by a whole row, measured from the layout as it is right now, so a phone's single column steps one card at a time. icon is an element, so pass <IconRocket />. The count is written with locale. The selected panel is a tab stop, so it shows a focus ring when the keyboard reaches it.

items.name: card-tabs-demo
items.title: Card tabs demo
items.description: A working preview of Card tabs.

items.name: responsive-dialog
items.title: Responsive dialog
items.description: One dialog API that is a centred modal on desktop and a bottom drawer on phones, switching live without losing the content's state.
items.docs: Pass title and description (both required, and both wired into either shape), a trigger, the children and an optional footer, then open and onOpenChange to control it or leave them out. It is one element that changes shape, not two components: above breakpoint (640px by default) it is a centred dialog, below it a bottom drawer with a grab handle that closes on a drag past a third of its height or a quick flick; resize or rotate while it is open and nothing in the children is remounted, so typed text and scroll positions stay. Tall children scroll in the body while the title and the footer stay; the footer pads for the home indicator in the drawer (the page needs viewport-fit=cover in its viewport meta for that inset to have a value). Focus lands on a child marked data-autofocus, else on the first field, else on the title, and returns to the trigger on close. dismissible={false} turns off Escape, an outside tap, the close button and the drag, so only your own buttons close it. The viewport is read after mount, so server and browser markup agree.

items.name: responsive-dialog-demo
items.title: Responsive dialog demo
items.description: A working preview of Responsive dialog.

items.name: choice-dialog
items.title: Choice dialog
items.description: A dialog for choosing between outcomes, not just yes or no: radio options with a line of consequence each, the safest preselected, and a confirm that names the choice.
items.docs: Pass title, description, options (id, label, description, destructive) and onConfirm(id, { remember }), plus a trigger, or open and onOpenChange to control it. The options are a radio group: arrow keys move, and Enter confirms. The first option that is not destructive is selected when it opens, so the safe answer is already chosen; defaultValue picks another. A destructive option takes the destructive style only while it is selected, and the confirm button follows it. confirmLabel is a string or a function of the chosen option, so the button reads "Delete all events"; without it the button repeats the option's label. rememberLabel adds a checkbox whose state is passed to onConfirm. Return a promise from onConfirm: while it is pending the whole dialog is locked, Escape and outside clicks included, and the button shows a spinner; when it resolves the dialog closes, and when it rejects the error message shows inside the dialog, which stays open for another try, and focus returns to the control that was pressed. The panel is never taller than the screen: the title and the buttons stay in view and the options scroll between them, so on a phone held sideways Confirm is still in reach. Nothing chosen last time is carried into the next opening.

items.name: choice-dialog-demo
items.title: Choice dialog demo
items.description: A working preview of Choice dialog.

items.name: selectable-table
items.title: Selectable table
items.description: Row selection for a table: a checkbox per row, a select-all header with a mixed state, Shift-click ranges, rows that say why they cannot be picked, and a live count.
items.docs: Give it columns, rows and getRowId, then hold the ids in a Set: selected and onSelectedChange. The header checkbox acts on the rows on screen and keeps ids that are not on screen, so a selection can span pages. Shift-click picks the range between two rows; return a sentence from isRowDisabled to say why a row cannot be picked (the box stays reachable by keyboard). Pass getRowLabel so each checkbox is named for its row. Pair it with SelectionBanner to offer every row across pages.

items.name: selectable-table-demo
items.title: Selectable table demo
items.description: A working preview of Selectable table.

items.name: row-actions-menu
items.title: Row actions menu
items.description: The three-dot menu at the end of a row: named for its row, grouped actions, disabled items that say why, and a destructive item that asks first.
items.docs: label names the row ('Invoice 1042'), so the trigger reads 'Actions for Invoice 1042'. actions is a list of { id, label, icon, shortcut, group, destructive, disabled, disabledReason }; groups are divided by rules in the order they first appear. A destructive action opens a confirm popover next to the button and calls onAction only after the confirm. contextMenu also opens the menu on a right-click anywhere on the row and on Shift+F10; the row is the closest tr, [role=row] or li, and a link or a field keeps the browser's own menu. Shortcuts are display only. After a confirmed delete the row, and the focus that was on its button, are gone: move focus to the actions button of the next row yourself (the one above when it was the last, a restore link or the table when none are left). The demo does it with a layout effect keyed on the rows.

items.name: row-actions-menu-demo
items.title: Row actions menu demo
items.description: A working preview of Row actions menu.

items.name: selection-banner
items.title: Selection banner
items.description: The line under a table header that offers to select every row across all pages once the whole page is selected.
items.docs: Mount it when every row of the page is selected. It reads 'All 25 orders on this page are selected' with 'Select all 312 orders'; once allSelected is true it reads 'All 312 orders are selected' with 'Clear selection'. Keeping the 'everything matching the query' flag is yours, because only you know what all 312 means. It is one button that changes its words, so focus stays on it. Clear selection is the exception: it removes the banner and the button that had the focus, so in onClear move focus to the header checkbox of the table first (the demo does).

items.name: selection-banner-demo
items.title: Selection banner demo
items.description: A working preview of Selection banner.

items.name: table-states
items.title: Table states
items.description: The four states of a table body, loading, empty, no results after filtering and a failed load with retry, all kept inside the table.
items.docs: Put TableBodyState where the TableBody would be: it renders its own tbody, so the header stays put from one state to the next. For the columns to hold their widths when the rows arrive too, give the table table-fixed and widths on its header cells (w-28 and so on, one column left automatic): a table that sizes its columns to what is in them re-flows when that changes, and no body can prevent it. Give columnCount the number of columns and rowCount about a page of rows, so loading takes the height the rows will. A message is one cell across all columns; its words reach a screen reader through a status region that exists before the words do. filters names the active filters in the filtered-empty state; onClear and onRetry add the buttons. Retry and Clear filters are removed by the state they cause, so while the body stays mounted it takes the focus they had (it is focusable by script and is not a tab stop). When you swap it for your own rows, move focus yourself, to the table or its first row.

items.name: table-states-demo
items.title: Table states demo
items.description: A working preview of Table states.

items.name: sticky-table
items.title: Sticky table
items.description: A table in its own scroll area with a sticky header and a pinned first column, edge shadows appearing only when there is more to scroll.
items.docs: Pass the Table parts (TableHeader, TableBody, TableFooter) as children, not a Table, and a label for the scroll box. maxHeight sets where rows start to scroll under the header; stickyColumns pins up to three leading columns. A table scrolls sideways only when its columns want more room than the box has: give it a min-w through tableClassName or its cells whitespace-nowrap. scrollRef reaches the scrolling box.

items.name: sticky-table-demo
items.title: Sticky table demo
items.description: A working preview of Sticky table.

items.name: responsive-table
items.title: Responsive table
items.description: A table that turns into stacked label and value cards when its own box is narrow, with the table semantics kept for screen readers.
items.docs: Below 40rem of its own width each row is a card; the switch is a container query, so a sidebar, a dialog and a page behave alike. header must be plain text, because it is also the label in front of a value in a card. priority 2 and 3 columns leave the table as the box narrows (below 48rem and 60rem) and always show in a card. primary names the column that becomes the title and the row header; getRowHref turns it into a link, or the whole card in the card layout. Give it a box with a width: a flex item needs w-full or min-w-0.

items.name: responsive-table-demo
items.title: Responsive table demo
items.description: A working preview of Responsive table.

items.name: numeric-table
items.title: Numeric table
items.description: A table of figures set properly: right-aligned tabular numbers, units in the header, readable negatives and a totals row.
items.docs: Columns declare kind (number, currency, percent or text), precision and unit; percent values are fractions. Figures are written by Intl for the locale you give, with a true minus sign and the word 'negative' for a screen reader. mark: 'highest', 'lowest' or 'both' marks a column's extremes with an arrow and words. total: 'sum', 'average' or a function fills the tfoot row; missing values read 'no data' and are left out of the sums, never counted as zero. The helpers in format.ts work on the server too.

items.name: numeric-table-demo
items.title: Numeric table demo
items.description: A working preview of Numeric table.

items.name: expandable-table
items.title: Expandable table
items.description: A table whose rows open a detail panel underneath: one button per row, aria-expanded and an expand-all control.
items.docs: renderDetail(row) draws the panel, a row of its own that spans every column. Each row's button is named 'Expand row {label}' (give getRowLabel) with aria-expanded and aria-controls; a closed panel is aria-hidden and inert, and opening eases the height unless reduced motion is on. expanded and onExpandedChange hold the open ids as a Set; mode 'single' keeps one open and drops the expand-all button, which otherwise shows a mixed state while only some rows are open.

items.name: expandable-table-demo
items.title: Expandable table demo
items.description: A working preview of Expandable table.

items.name: key-value-list
items.title: Key value list
items.description: Technical facts you copy: IDs, URLs and hashes in mono, a copy button per row, long values cut in the middle, secrets masked.
items.docs: items are { label, value, copyable, mono, secret, href }. It is the description list's dl markup, so a screen reader hears the same terms and values. A copyable row's button is named 'Copy order ID' and confirms with 'Copied order ID'; a secret stays dots until its reveal button is pressed and hides again after hideSecretsAfter seconds; a long string value gives up its middle, with the whole text in a tooltip and for a screen reader. A value with an href is underlined at rest, and a link to another site (https://) carries a small arrow. A secret needs a string value: any other node stays dots with no reveal button, and development logs an error. layout 'columns' puts the labels beside the values once the list is 28rem wide; it measures its own width, so give it a box that has one.

items.name: key-value-list-demo
items.title: Key value list demo
items.description: A working preview of Key value list.

items.name: table-density-toggle
items.title: Table density toggle
items.description: Compact, comfortable or spacious rows: a small segmented control plus a context that every table cell reads.
items.docs: Wrap the tables and the control in TableDensityProvider. It sets data-density on a display: contents wrapper and every td and th below takes its height (32, 44 or 56px) and text size from it, whether it comes from this kit's Table or a plain table. value, onValueChange, defaultValue and storageKey work as in any controlled field; with storageKey the choice is remembered, the first render uses defaultValue and the stored choice follows. useTableDensity() gives a cell of your own the density. A cell that sets its own height and padding (a panel that spans the table, a message) opts out with data-density-skip, and so does everything inside it: a table in an expandable panel keeps its own sizes. The control takes what a div takes (id, aria-*, data-*) for the group of three.

items.name: table-density-toggle-demo
items.title: Table density toggle demo
items.description: A working preview of Table density toggle.

items.name: unsaved-changes-dialog
items.title: Unsaved changes dialog
items.description: The question before leaving a form with changes: Save, Discard or Keep editing, with a guard hook for link clicks, the Back button and the browser's own prompt.
items.docs: The dialog is only the question and useLeaveGuard(dirty) is the guard; either works alone. Spread guard.dialogProps onto the dialog and give it onSave: resolve true (or nothing) to save and leave, resolve false or throw to stay open and show why. Without onSave there are two answers and Discard turns solid. The guard catches a link click before your router and clicks the link again on leave; it catches Back with one extra history entry of its own; and it registers the browser's own prompt for closing the tab or reloading. A router.push from a button cannot be seen: wrap it in guard.request(() => router.push(url)). The extra entry has a cost: while there are changes the page is in the history twice, and a leave through a link or request first steps back off it (your router sees a Back to the same page), so the history stays page, next page.

items.name: unsaved-changes-dialog-demo
items.title: Unsaved changes dialog demo
items.description: A working preview of Unsaved changes dialog.

items.name: progress-dialog
items.title: Progress dialog
items.description: A modal for a long task: a real progress bar read out every ten percent, the step in words, a cancel that asks once, and a done or failed end state in place.
items.docs: Set status to running, done, failed or cancelled and the body follows in place; focus moves to the primary button of the end state. progress runs from 0 to 1, and leaving it out gives a bar with no length. The bar is announced politely every ten percent, and a step label that is the only news at most every five seconds. onCancel runs after the person confirms the question; you set status to cancelled when it is carried out. onBackground hands the task back to the page: close the dialog and show your own banner. result is the body of the done state, with its next action; error and onRetry belong to the failed one. Escape and a click outside never close a running task.

items.name: progress-dialog-demo
items.title: Progress dialog demo
items.description: A working preview of Progress dialog.

items.name: action-sheet
items.title: Action sheet
items.description: The mobile list of actions that rises from the bottom edge: large rows, a destructive row last, a separate Cancel, menu keys, and a narrow dialog on wide screens.
items.docs: actions are plain objects: label, icon (an element), onSelect, destructive, disabled and description. Destructive rows are moved to the end. The list is a menu: one tab stop, the arrow keys, Home, End and type-ahead; a disabled row stays reachable so its description can say why. Below 640px (breakpoint), and on any screen under 560px tall such as a phone held sideways, it is a Drawer, so a drag on the handle or a tap on the backdrop dismisses it; from 640px wide on a taller screen it is a narrow Dialog with the same list. In both the rows scroll when the screen is too short for them and the Cancel stays in view. With a trigger, focus goes back to it on close; without one (open with `open`) give focus back yourself in onOpenChange. For more than about seven choices use a menu or a list instead.

items.name: action-sheet-demo
items.title: Action sheet demo
items.description: A working preview of Action sheet.

items.name: form-sheet
items.title: Form sheet
items.description: A side sheet built for editing: header and footer in view, a scrolling body with edge shadows, a Discard changes? guard, and a problem summary after a failed save.
items.docs: onSubmit receives the form's FormData. To fail, return a list of { field, message } or throw an Error: the sheet stays open with a summary at the top and focus on the first invalid field, so mark invalid controls aria-invalid="true". dirty makes closing by the corner button, Cancel, Escape or the backdrop ask Discard changes? first, and Keep editing puts focus back where it was. While onSubmit is pending (or pending is true) the fields, which sit in one fieldset, and the close button are locked, and the Save button says it is busy. side is right or left on a wide screen and a bottom sheet on a phone.

items.name: form-sheet-demo
items.title: Form sheet demo
items.description: A working preview of Form sheet.

items.name: help-popover
items.title: Help popover
items.description: The small question-mark button beside a label that opens a short explanation with a link or two, for touch, keyboard and screen readers.
items.docs: label is required: it names the button after what it explains (Help: API rate limit). With side="auto" the popover opens to the right of the field when the label next to the button names one (label for) and there is room, above the label otherwise, and below the field when there is no room above either, so it does not sit on the field. The content can be paragraphs, a list, strong text or a short code sample, which wraps instead of scrolling. A link with external opens in a new tab with noopener and says so to screen readers. It is a non-modal popover: Escape closes it, focus returns to the button, and opening another help button closes the first.

items.name: help-popover-demo
items.title: Help popover demo
items.description: A working preview of Help popover.

items.name: truncate-tooltip
items.title: Truncate tooltip
items.description: Text that ends in an ellipsis and shows the full text in a tooltip only when it is actually cut off, by hover, keyboard focus or a tap.
items.docs: Give it a width to work in: a flex child with min-w-0, a table cell in a fixed layout, or a box with a maximum width. lines sets a clamp to that many lines. It measures after layout, on resize and when web fonts arrive, and only a cut-off text gets the tooltip and a tab stop, so a table of names adds no tab stop to rows that fit. The text stays whole in the DOM, so screen readers and copy get all of it. On touch a tap toggles the tooltip.

items.name: truncate-tooltip-demo
items.title: Truncate tooltip demo
items.description: A working preview of Truncate tooltip.

items.name: go-to-dialog
items.title: Go to dialog
items.description: Jump to a page, line, row or date from the keyboard: a one-field dialog opened by a shortcut, with the range as its hint, as-you-type checks and Enter to go.
items.docs: kind is number or date. A number is checked as it is typed (whole numbers, between min and max) and named in words; a date is the library's DateField in the order the locale writes it. min, max and defaultValue are numbers, or ISO dates for a date. onGo runs once the dialog has closed and given focus back, so you can move focus to where you went. shortcut defaults to mod+g (Command on a Mac, Control elsewhere), is ignored while someone types in another field or another modal is open, and false turns it off. validate.ts has checkNumber, to run the same check on the server.

items.name: go-to-dialog-demo
items.title: Go to dialog demo
items.description: A working preview of Go to dialog.

items.name: video-dialog
items.title: Video dialog
items.description: Watch the video in a dialog: a poster with a play button opens a player at the video's proportions that starts on open, stops on close and returns focus.
items.docs: title is required: it is the dialog's title and names the player and the iframe. Give sources (best first, with their type) or an embedUrl. The player exists only while the dialog is open: it starts when the browser allows sound, otherwise muted with a hint to turn it on, and it is paused the moment the dialog closes. An embedUrl is shown in a titled iframe that is created after the dialog opens; only http, https and your own paths are used, and your Content-Security-Policy must allow the host in frame-src. trigger is any single element: leave it out for a poster button, pass null to open it yourself with open. The open animation is skipped under reduced motion.

items.name: video-dialog-demo
items.title: Video dialog demo
items.description: A working preview of Video dialog.

items.name: cell-preview-popover
items.title: Cell preview popover
items.description: Peek at the full value of a cut-off table cell: long text, a JSON blob or a URL in a scrollable monospaced popover with Copy.
items.docs: Use it in a table with table-fixed, or in any box with a width. kind is text, json (pretty-printed, keys in a quieter grey) or url (a link that opens a new tab; only http and https addresses become links). maxLines is how many lines the cell shows before the ellipsis. children replaces what the cell shows; the popover still shows the value. The expand mark appears only when the text is cut off. The cell is a button with aria-expanded; Escape closes the popover. The popover is never taller than the room the screen leaves: the value scrolls inside it and Copy stays in view. format.ts has fullText and cellText for the server.

items.name: cell-preview-popover-demo
items.title: Cell preview popover demo
items.description: A working preview of Cell preview popover.

items.name: sortable-table
items.title: Sortable table
items.description: A table driven by a column list that sorts on header click, with aria-sort on the active header, a stable order, and text, numbers and dates each compared the right way.
items.docs: columns take key, header, align, sortType (text, number or date, or false for no sort), accessor and cell; a header cycles ascending, descending, off. Text is ordered by Intl.Collator for the locale with numbers in natural order, numbers and ISO dates by value, empty values are always last and equal rows keep their order. Only the sorted header has aria-sort, and a polite line says what changed. Use getRowId for stable keys, and sort (with onSortChange) or defaultSort. cell and accessor are functions, so render it from a client component. sort.ts has sortRows for sorting on the server.

items.name: sortable-table-demo
items.title: Sortable table demo
items.description: A working preview of Sortable table.

items.name: column-header-menu
items.title: Column header menu
items.description: A column header with a menu: sort ascending or descending, clear the sort, hide the column, pin it left or right. Each group shows only when you pass its callback.
items.docs: Use it as the header cell of a column: give it the label, the current sort and the callbacks you support, and the menu shows only those groups. It sets aria-sort on the th itself while the column is sorted, so never add it yourself. Hiding removes the button, so move the focus to the table afterwards. Pinning only reports the edge: the sticky positioning is yours.

items.name: column-header-menu-demo
items.title: Column header menu demo
items.description: A working preview of Column header menu.

items.name: table-cells
items.title: Table cells
items.description: The seven cells every table needs, aligned and truncating correctly: person, date, money, status, progress, tags and actions.
items.docs: Put each cell inside a TableCell and give it plain values: IdentityCell a name, DateCell a date with a locale and time zone, MoneyCell an amount and a currency. Pass now to DateCell when the text must read the same every time. Give the header of a money or number column text-right, and change where a cell truncates with a max-width class. IdentityCell keeps its avatar at one size with or without a detail line (size sm, default or lg), so a column of people stays straight.

items.name: table-cells-demo
items.title: Table cells demo
items.description: A working preview of Table cells.

items.name: linked-row-table
items.title: Linked row table
items.description: Whole-row navigation done right: one real link per row, buttons inside still work, and Cmd-click opens a new tab.
items.docs: Give it columns, rows, getRowHref and the key of the column that holds the name of the row, which becomes the link. Mark columns with buttons, checkboxes or menus as interactive so they sit above the link. Use onRowClick to route on the client; a Cmd, Ctrl or middle click still opens the address in a new tab. Because the link covers the row, text in it cannot be selected. className goes to the box around the table and tableClassName to the table itself; the other props (aria-label, id) go to the table.

items.name: linked-row-table-demo
items.title: Linked row table demo
items.description: A working preview of Linked row table.

items.name: editable-cell
items.title: Editable cell
items.description: A table cell that edits in place like a spreadsheet: Enter to edit, Enter to save, Escape to cancel, with validation and a saving state.
items.docs: Put it in a TableCell with a value, a label and onCommit. Return a promise from onCommit to show the saving state; reject with an Error whose message is written for people, and the old value comes back with that line under it. Use type number or select for those fields, and validate to refuse a value with a message that shows under the cell. The cell follows value whenever it changes. A mouse starts an edit with a double-click, Enter or F2, and says so on hover; a tap starts it at once on a touch screen.

items.name: editable-cell-demo
items.title: Editable cell demo
items.description: A working preview of Editable cell.

items.name: grouped-list
items.title: Grouped list
items.description: A long list under sticky group headers (days, letters, teams) with counts and an optional A to Z jump rail.
items.docs: Give it groups of items, a renderItem function and a height such as h-96, because it scrolls inside. The id of a group can be a date: pass getGroupLabel to write it as Today or Yesterday. Turn on indexRail for alphabetical lists; groups with no items are left out, so the rail has no empty letters. The rail is one Tab stop: Up, Down, Home and End walk its letters, Enter or Space jump. Each button is 24 pixels tall, so give the list about 24 pixels per group (h-[34rem] for A to Z) or the rail scrolls.

items.name: grouped-list-demo
items.title: Grouped list demo
items.description: A working preview of Grouped list.

items.name: pinnable-list
items.title: Pinnable list
items.description: A list where items can be pinned to the top: a Pinned group, a pin toggle on each row and an order you control.
items.docs: Give it items with an id and a label, and hold the pinned ids yourself (pinned and onPinnedChange) or let it hold them (defaultPinned). The order of items is the order inside each group. Set maxPinned to cap it: at the limit the other pin buttons switch off and the reason is written under the group title.

items.name: pinnable-list-demo
items.title: Pinnable list demo
items.description: A working preview of Pinnable list.

items.name: table-export-menu
items.title: Table export menu
items.description: An Export menu for any table: download the rows as CSV or copy them for a spreadsheet, with no server involved.
items.docs: Describe the file with columns (a key, a header and an optional exportValue for raw values) and pass rows, or getRows to build them only when asked. The file is built in the browser: UTF-8 with a byte order mark for Excel, quotes escaped, hidden columns skipped. Use a semicolon delimiter for locales that write decimals with a comma, and onExported to show your own toast. After an export the button shows a check and one short word for a moment (the labels downloadedShort, copiedShort and so on), so the toolbar does not move; the whole line is announced to screen readers and set as the title.

items.name: table-export-menu-demo
items.title: Table export menu demo
items.description: A working preview of Table export menu.

items.name: table-column-resizer
items.title: Table column resizer
items.description: A drag handle for a column header that resizes with the pointer or arrow keys, with limits, a reset and a live width.
items.docs: Place it inside a TableHead with className relative, hold the width in state and pass it as width and onWidthChange. Put the same width on the header cell and set table-layout fixed on the table, with a table width that is the sum of its columns. Pass defaultWidth so Enter and a double-click can reset the column, and onResizeEnd to save the widths. The handle of the last column stays inside its cell, so the table is never wider than the sum of its columns. Left and Right move 8 pixels (32 with Shift), Home and End go to the limits.

items.name: table-column-resizer-demo
items.title: Table column resizer demo
items.description: A working preview of Table column resizer.

items.name: column-group-table
items.title: Column group table
items.description: A table with grouped column headers: spanning headers over sub-columns, built with proper scope so screen readers still hear them.
items.docs: Give it columnGroups (an id, a label and columns), rows and an optional rowHeader. Give a group a summary column key and it can be folded down to that column. Pass label to name the scroll box and a caption to say what the figures are. Columns read row[key]; use accessor and cell for anything else. With a rowHeader, the label of a group and its button stay beside the row names while the group's columns scroll under them.

items.name: column-group-table-demo
items.title: Column group table demo
items.description: A working preview of Column group table.

items.name: navigable-grid
items.title: Navigable grid
items.description: A table with the spreadsheet keyboard model: arrow keys between cells, Home and End along a row, one cell in the tab order, and Enter to reach the controls inside.
items.docs: Give it columns and rows and name it with a caption or an aria-label. The grid is one Tab stop: arrows move one cell, Home and End go to the ends of the row, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End to the corners, PageUp and PageDown by a screenful. Buttons, checkboxes and inputs in cells leave the Tab order until you press Enter or F2 on their cell; Escape hands the focus back, and Tab walks that cell's controls and then leaves the grid. Mark the column that names the row with rowHeader, read where the person is from onCellFocus, and hide columns with CSS if you like: the keyboard steps over them. Keep columns the same array between renders and moving the cursor redraws two rows, not all of them.

items.name: navigable-grid-demo
items.title: Navigable grid demo
items.description: A working preview of Navigable grid.

items.name: icons
items.title: Icons
items.description: The RHS UI icon set: one drawing hand for every glyph, a 1.75px stroke on a 24 grid with the open corner as its signature. Sized by size, coloured by currentColor, with Glyph to draw your own.
items.docs: Import the glyphs you need from "@rhs-ui/icons". Pass a title when an icon is the only label. Draw your own glyph in the same hand with <Glyph d="..." />.

items.name: animated-icon
items.title: Animated icon
items.description: The engine behind the animated icons: hover, focus, loop and first-view triggers through the Web Animations API, a two-state frame in plain CSS, and reduced motion respected. No animation library.
items.docs: Installed with every animated icon. Motion icons take trigger: hover (default, follows the button or link around the icon), loop, appear or static. State icons take active.

items.name: animated-icon-demo
items.title: Animated icon demo
items.description: Animated icons in buttons: a bell on hover, a refresh that loops while syncing, and a copy icon that turns into a check.

items.name: animated-bell
items.title: Animated bell
items.description: A bell that rings: the body swings from its crown and the clapper follows a beat later. For notifications and reminders.
items.docs: Inside a Button it rings when the button is hovered or focused. Use trigger="loop" while there are unread notifications.

items.name: animated-search
items.title: Animated search
items.description: A lens that looks left and right before it settles. For search, filter and lookup actions.
items.docs: Use trigger="loop" while results are loading.

items.name: animated-arrow-right
items.title: Animated arrow right
items.description: An arrow that leaves on the right and comes back in from the left. For continue, next and call-to-action buttons.
items.docs: Place it after the label: <Button>Continue <IconArrowRightAnimated /></Button>.

items.name: animated-heart
items.title: Animated heart
items.description: A heart that beats twice, the second beat softer than the first. For favourites, wishlists and likes.

meta.usage:
<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Save to wishlist" aria-pressed={saved}>
  <IconHeartAnimated />
</Button>

items.docs: Pair it with aria-pressed on the wishlist button; the icon only shows the gesture.

items.name: animated-sparkle
items.title: Animated sparkle
items.description: A four-point star that turns a quarter and lands on itself while the small star pops back in. For new, highlight and AI states.
items.docs: Use trigger="loop" sparingly: one moving sparkle on a page is a highlight, three is noise.

items.name: animated-refresh
items.title: Animated refresh
items.description: One eased full turn on hover, or a steady loop while something syncs.
items.docs: Switch to trigger="loop" while syncing and set aria-busy on the button; it finishes its turn when you switch back.

items.name: animated-download
items.title: Animated download
items.description: The arrow drops through the tray and comes back from the top while the tray gives a little. For download and export actions.
items.docs: Inside a download link it plays on hover and on keyboard focus of the link.

items.name: animated-trash
items.title: Animated trash
items.description: The lid lifts from its left hinge and drops shut. For delete and remove actions.
items.docs: An icon-only delete button still needs an accessible label: <Button size="icon" aria-label="Delete">.

items.name: animated-send
items.title: Animated send
items.description: A paper plane that flies off to the top right and glides back in from the bottom left. For send, share and submit.
items.docs: Plays on hover and focus of the submit button it sits in.

items.name: animated-cart
items.title: Animated cart
items.description: A product drops into the basket and the cart dips under its weight. For add-to-cart buttons and cart links.
items.docs: At rest it is the cart glyph; the product only shows while it moves.

items.name: animated-check-circle
items.title: Animated check circle
items.description: The ring draws itself and then the check. For success states, best with trigger appear.

meta.usage: Your order is confirmed.

items.docs: <IconCheckCircleAnimated trigger="appear" /> draws once when a confirmation scrolls into view.

items.name: animated-copy
items.title: Animated copy
items.description: A copy icon that turns into a drawn check while active. For confirming a copy to the clipboard.
items.docs: Set active for a moment after navigator.clipboard.writeText resolves, and announce it in a live region.

items.name: animated-menu
items.title: Animated menu
items.description: Three lines that fold into a cross while active. For the open state of a navigation menu.

meta.usage:
<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Menu" aria-expanded={open} onClick={toggle}>
  <IconMenuAnimated active={open} />
</Button>

items.docs: Bind active to the menu's open state and aria-expanded on the button.

items.name: animated-sun-moon
items.title: Animated sun and moon
items.description: The sun draws in its rays and turns into the moon while active. For a light and dark theme switch.

meta.usage:
<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Dark theme" aria-pressed={dark} onClick={toggleTheme}>
  <IconSunMoonAnimated active={dark} />
</Button>

items.docs: Bind active to the resolved theme after hydration, so the server and the first client render agree.

items.name: animated-settings
items.title: Animated settings
items.description: A gear that turns one tooth and settles while the hub gives a little. For settings and preferences.
items.docs: Inside a settings button it turns on hover and on keyboard focus. Use trigger="loop" while preferences are saving.

items.name: animated-mail
items.title: Animated mail
items.description: The flap folds open and a letter rises out before everything closes again. For mail, invites and messages.
items.docs: Use it in a contact or invite action; trigger="appear" plays it once when the section scrolls into view.

items.name: animated-upload
items.title: Animated upload
items.description: The arrow leaves through the top and comes back from the tray, which gives under it. For upload and import actions.
items.docs: Switch to trigger="loop" while a file is uploading and set aria-busy on the button.

items.name: animated-star
items.title: Animated star
items.description: A fifth of a turn lands the star back on itself, with a pop at the end. For ratings, favourites and highlights.

meta.usage:
<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Add to favourites" aria-pressed={starred}>
  <IconStarAnimated />
</Button>

items.docs: Pair it with aria-pressed on a favourite button; the icon shows the gesture, the button holds the state.

items.name: animated-log-out
items.title: Animated log out
items.description: The arrow leaves through the door and comes back in behind it. For sign out and leave actions.
items.docs: Inside a sign-out button it plays on hover and on keyboard focus of that button.

items.name: animated-phone
items.title: Animated phone
items.description: A handset that rings: a shake that dies out. For call actions and contact details.
items.docs: Use trigger="loop" for an incoming call and stop the loop the moment it is answered.

items.name: animated-clock
items.title: Animated clock
items.description: Time passing: the minute hand makes two turns while the hour hand makes one. For schedules, history and timers.
items.docs: Use trigger="loop" while something is pending, or trigger="appear" on a history panel.

items.name: animated-message
items.title: Animated message
items.description: Three dots type inside the bubble and leave it empty again. For chat, comments and support.
items.docs: Use trigger="loop" as a typing indicator and announce the same thing in a live region.

items.name: animated-lock
items.title: Animated lock
items.description: A padlock that springs open. For locked and unlocked states.
items.docs: Set active when whatever it guards is unlocked, and mirror that in the button label or aria-pressed.

items.name: animated-eye
items.title: Animated eye
items.description: The eye closes behind a line that draws itself. For showing and hiding a password or a value.

meta.usage:
<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label={shown ? "Hide password" : "Show password"} onClick={toggle}>
  <IconEyeAnimated active={shown} />
</Button>

items.docs: Set active when the content is hidden; the button label should change with it (Show password, Hide password).

items.name: animated-play-pause
items.title: Animated play and pause
items.description: Play turns into pause and back. For media and any start and stop control.
items.docs: Set active while something is playing, and keep the accessible name in step (Play, Pause).

items.name: animated-plus
items.title: Animated plus
items.description: A plus that turns an eighth of a turn into a close. For add buttons that open something.

meta.usage:
<Button size="icon" aria-label="New item" aria-expanded={open} onClick={toggle}>
  <IconPlusAnimated active={open} />
</Button>

items.docs: Bind active to the open state of the menu or panel it toggles, next to aria-expanded.

items.name: animated-bookmark
items.title: Animated bookmark
items.description: The ribbon fills and drops into place. For saving an item for later.

meta.usage:
<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Save for later" aria-pressed={saved} onClick={save}>
  <IconBookmarkAnimated active={saved} />
</Button>

items.docs: Set active when the item is saved and use aria-pressed on the button around it.

items.title: Animated price

items.name: product-card
items.title: Product card
