items.description: One plan as a card: its price and interval, what it includes and the button, with 'Most popular' and 'Your plan' told in words, not only in colour.
items.docs: Pass the plan's name, a description and the price as { amount, interval, currency, note }. amount is in minor units (2900 is 29.00; a string such as 'Custom' is shown as written), interval is muted after a slash ('/ month') and note is the small line under it ('€288 billed yearly'). A price that changes, as it does when a billing toggle flips, counts to its new value, and a whole price drops its cents. features take plain strings, or { label, included: false } for a feature the plan leaves out, which a screen reader hears as 'Not included'. cta is { label, href?, onClick?, disabled?, loading? }; with an href it renders as a link that needs no JavaScript, and a label too long for the button wraps onto a second line and the button grows with it instead of being cut off. recommended draws a heavier border and the pill 'Most popular' (badge replaces its words, and also works on a card that is not recommended); current replaces the button with 'Your plan' and sets aria-current. locale writes the price, headingAs sets the heading level (h3 by default) and labels holds the fixed words for another language. It keeps no state and renders on the server.

items.name: plan-card-demo
items.title: Plan card demo
items.description: A working preview of Plan card.

items.name: booking-summary
items.title: Booking summary
items.description: What you are about to book, as a list: service, date and time, who and where, the total set apart, and an edit link on every row.
items.docs: service and staff can be plain strings or objects ({ name, detail }, { name, role }); location is { name, address: [lines] } and is set in an <address> element. start is an ISO date-time, a Date or a timestamp and duration is in minutes: the row reads 'Tuesday 3 November 2026' with '10:00 to 11:00 · 1 hour' under it, written in locale and timeZone (pass both, so the server and the browser agree). price is { amount, currency, note? } with the amount in the currency's own minor units (9500 is 95.00 EUR, but 9,500 JPY, which has none) and is set apart in the footer; policy is the cancellation policy as one plain line under it. onEdit(part) adds an 'Edit' button to every row, and editHrefs makes a part a real link instead; without either the summary is read-only, as on a confirmation page. Each link is named for what it changes, from labels and not from the row's term: editService, editDateTime, editStaff, editLocation and editNotes ('Edit service', 'Edit date and time', 'Edit staff member', 'Edit location', 'Edit notes'), so the rows 'With' and 'Where' are never announced as 'Edit with' and 'Edit where'. Keep the visible word (labels.edit) inside each name when you translate them, so voice control matches what is on screen. confirmed adds a check mark and the heading 'Booking confirmed', and reference prints the booking reference. headingAs sets the heading level (h2 by default) and labels holds the fixed words for another language. It keeps no state and renders on the server.

items.name: booking-summary-demo
items.title: Booking summary demo
items.description: A working preview of Booking summary.

items.name: coupon-card
items.title: Coupon card
items.description: A voucher: the offer, its code with a copy button, the conditions and the expiry, on a card with a perforated edge.
items.docs: offer is the headline on the stub ('20% off'), code the voucher code, description what it applies to and conditions the small print as a list behind a 'Details' disclosure. expiresAt is a date-only string such as '2026-10-29' (valid through the end of that day in timeZone) or a date-time; the card writes it out ('Expires in 3 days', 'Expires today', 'Expired 8 days ago') with the full date in a tooltip that hover, tap and keyboard focus open. Pass now from the server so the first render already says it; without it the card writes the plain date until the browser's clock is known, then switches. status is 'active', 'used' or 'expired': the last two mute the card, strike the code through and take the copy button away, and an active coupon past its date is shown as expired. onCopy(code) is called once the code is on the clipboard, and the copy button confirms through a polite live region. A code that does not fit beside the button keeps its letters together and the button drops under it; only a code longer than the whole row ever breaks. The notches are mask cut-outs, so the page shows through in light and dark. The layout follows the card's own width: stacked below 32rem, stub and body side by side above it. labels holds every fixed word.

items.name: coupon-card-demo
items.title: Coupon card demo
items.description: A working preview of Coupon card.

items.name: room-card
items.title: Room card
items.description: A hotel room or rental: photos, size and beds, amenities, the price per night and the stay total, with 'Only 2 left' and sold-out states in words.
items.docs: name, beds ('1 king bed'), size ('28 m²') and sleeps describe the room; images are { src, alt } and show in a slider with arrows (on hover and focus, always on touch), native swipe and a loop. amenities lists the first maxAmenities (4) with a check mark; the 'See all 9 amenities' link appears when amenitiesHref (a real link) or onSeeAllAmenities (a callback) gives it somewhere to go, and without either every amenity is listed. pricePerNight and totalPrice are in minor units; nights writes 'for 2 nights' beside the total, and taxesIncluded (default true) chooses between 'taxes included' and 'plus taxes'. refundable says 'Free cancellation' or 'Non-refundable', and roomsLeft shows 'Only 2 left' at lowStockAt (3) or fewer; 0 turns the price into 'Not available for these dates' and disables the button, which points at that reason. onSelect is called by the button. The pictures sit on top in a narrow column and beside the details from 48rem. locale writes the prices, headingAs sets the heading level and labels holds every fixed word.

items.name: room-card-demo
items.title: Room card demo
items.description: A working preview of Room card.

items.name: course-card
items.title: Course card
items.description: A course in a catalogue: cover, level, instructor, length, rating and price with its discount in words, or progress and Continue once enrolled.
items.docs: title, cover ({ src, alt }), instructor ({ name, image? }), level ('beginner', 'intermediate' or 'advanced': a word with a three-bar glyph), duration (minutes, written '6h 30m'), lessons, rating, ratingCount, price (minor units; 0 says 'Free'), compareAtPrice (struck through, with '38% off' in words), badge and href. The whole card is one link, through the title, so there is a single tab stop and nothing nested in a link. progress (0 to 100) turns it into an enrolled course: a progress bar and 'Continue' replace the price, and at 100 it says 'Completed' and 'Review'. The stars are one image named 'Rated 4.8 out of 5 by 1,284 learners'. locale writes the numbers and prices, headingAs sets the heading level (h3 by default) and labels holds the fixed words. It keeps no state and renders on the server.

items.name: course-card-demo
items.title: Course card demo
items.description: A working preview of Course card.

items.name: price-quote-card
items.title: Price quote card
items.description: A price quote you received: number, validity, total with tax stated and its status, with accept and decline of equal weight, download and a way back when it expires.
items.docs: number, issuedAt, validUntil, total (in the currency's own minor units: 1452000 is 14,520.00 EUR, but 1,452,000 JPY, which has none), currency, taxIncluded (the rate in percent that the total includes: 21 says '21% VAT included', and labels.taxName renames the tax), status, supplier ({ name, contact? } or a string) and summary. validUntil is a date-only string (valid through the end of that day in timeZone) or a date-time, and the card says 'Valid until 30 Nov, 12 days left'. Pass now from the server for a first render that already counts the days; without it the card writes the plain date until the browser's clock is known. With now, the card's clock starts there, so a decision made in the card is stamped with now plus the time since it was given (a preview with a fixed now reads in its own time). An open quote (sent, viewed) past its date is shown as expired. Accept and decline are equal buttons that each ask once in a popover that keeps a gutter from the screen's edge on a phone (labels.cancel is its cancel button); onAccept and onDecline may return a promise (the popover shows the busy state, and if it rejects nothing is recorded and the card says so). Afterwards the card shows the outcome and when (decidedAt, or the moment of the click) and moves the keyboard focus to that line, because the buttons that held it are gone; a status that arrives from the page does not move the focus. An expired quote disables both and shows 'Ask for a new quote' for onRequestNew; onDownload adds 'Download PDF'. locale and timeZone write the dates, and labels holds every fixed word.

items.name: price-quote-card-demo
items.title: Price quote card demo
items.description: A working preview of Price quote card.

items.name: flight-card
items.title: Flight card
items.description: A flight option: departure and arrival in each airport's own time, duration and stops in words, airline, price and a select action, with every segment on demand.
items.docs: segments are the flights of the trip in order: { from, to, departure, arrival, carrier, flightNumber }, where from and to are airports { code, city?, timeZone } and the moments are ISO date-times with an offset or in UTC. Every time is written in its airport's own zone, with the abbreviation and the date in a tooltip (hover, tap or keyboard focus on the two main times). The route line says 'Direct', '1 stop in Zurich, 1h 20m' or '2 stops in Zurich and Madrid', shows a dot for every stop and the total duration (on a narrow card the duration joins the words under the line), and a landing on a later local day says '+1 day'. price is in minor units with priceNote ('per person'), cabin and baggage are plain strings and badge is a word in the corner ('Cheapest'). selected draws a heavier border and a button that says 'Selected'; onSelect is called by the button. The card's hidden heading names it by route, departure and airline ('Amsterdam to Lisbon, departs 07:25, Northwind Air': labels.title with {from}, {to}, {time} and {carrier}) and describes the button, so two flights on one route are told apart. 'Flight details' lists every segment with the layovers between them. Price and button sit beside the route from 36rem and below it on a narrow card. locale writes the times and the price, and labels holds every fixed word.

items.name: flight-card-demo
items.title: Flight card demo
items.description: A working preview of Flight card.

items.name: payment-card-preview
items.title: Payment card preview
items.description: A payment card drawn live as you fill in the form: number grouped by network, name and expiry, the brand in words, a back for the code, nothing stored.
items.docs: number, name, expiry, cvc and brand are whatever the form holds right now, complete or not: only digits count, so '4242 4242' and '4242-4242' are the same, and nothing is stored or sent. The brand is found from the first digits (visa, mastercard, amex, discover, diners, jcb, unionpay, maestro) unless you pass brand, which also takes any other text and sets it as it is; the digits group as the network groups them (4-4-4-4, 4-6-5 for American Express, 4-6-4 for Diners Club) and places still to be filled show as soft bullets. masked hides all but the last four digits (and the security code); flipped shows the back with the security code area, turning in 3D or cross-fading under reduced motion. The card is one figure whose accessible name tells what is filled in so far ('Visa card for Ada Lovelace ending 4242, expires 09/28'). The helpers in payment-card-preview/card (detectBrand, brandInfo, formatNumber, formatExpiry, digitsOf) format an input as the person types, which is how the demo uses them. The card scales with its width, so give it one with className. labels holds the fixed words. It keeps no state and renders on the server.

items.name: payment-card-preview-demo
items.title: Payment card preview demo
items.description: A working preview of Payment card preview.

items.name: discount-field
items.title: Discount field
items.description: A discount as either an amount or a percentage, with the switch inside the field and the resulting price shown against the original.
items.docs: A text field with a two-sided switch in it: your currency code ('EUR') and '%'. The number is read the way the switch says, and each side keeps its own number, so flipping never loses what was typed. value is { type: 'amount', value } in minor units or { type: 'percent', value } as a plain number, or null for an empty field; control it with value and onValueChange, or start it with defaultValue and defaultType. onValueChange gets null while the field is empty or the discount is refused, so a form never holds an impossible one. Pass price (minor units) and the field prints 'New price 38.40 EUR, 20% off' under itself (the percentage is worked out for an amount), and refuses an amount above the price or a percentage above maxPercent (100) in words, marking the input invalid. A comma or a point both work as the decimal separator, and the number is tidied when the field is left. name adds two hidden inputs for a plain form post: the number under name and its type under name-type. The switch is a radio group named 'Discount type' with arrow keys. locale writes the numbers, hideLabel keeps the label for screen readers only and labels holds the fixed words.

items.name: discount-field-demo
items.title: Discount field demo
items.description: A working preview of Discount field.

items.name: vat-price-field
items.title: VAT price field
items.description: Enter a price once and see both sides, with and without VAT, with a switch for which one you type and the VAT worked out between them.
items.docs: value is the amount as typed, in minor units (1240 is 12.40): the price without VAT when mode is 'excluding', the price with VAT when it is 'including'; mode and rate are controlled the same way, or start with defaultValue, defaultMode and defaultRate (the highest of rates). rates are percentages, 0, 9 and 21 unless you pass your own; a rate with decimals (7.7) works. onChange(price, input) gets { net, vat, gross, rate } in minor units, worked out in whole numbers and rounded half up exactly once so net + vat is always gross, or null for an empty field, and input is { value, mode, rate } to hand back when you control the field. Changing the switch keeps the typed number and works out the other side. currency sets the symbol and the decimals (two for euros, none for yen), a comma or a point both work as the decimal sign, and name adds hidden inputs for net, vat, gross and rate. A screen reader hears the result when the field is left or the switch or the rate changes. vat.ts exports fromNet, fromGross and vatPrice, so your server can work out the same numbers. locale writes the amounts and labels holds the fixed words, 'VAT {rate}' among them, for another language or another tax.

items.name: vat-price-field-demo
items.title: VAT price field demo
items.description: A working preview of VAT price field.

items.name: card-fieldset
items.title: Card fieldset
items.description: Card number, expiry and security code as one connected group with spacing, brand detection and a Luhn check, ready to swap for hosted fields.
items.docs: A frame for the card form, with no payment in it: nothing is stored, logged or sent, and the inputs have no name, so a surrounding form cannot post them. onChange(value, state) gets { number, expiry, code, name } (number is digits only, expiry is 'MM/YY') and { brand, valid }; control it with value or start it with defaultValue. The number is spaced as you type (4-4-4-4, or 4-6-5 for American Express), the network is named in words beside the field, and the length of the code follows it. The Luhn check, a month from 01 to 12 and 'not in the past' run when a field is left, each message tied to its input with aria-describedby and aria-invalid; a message that shows follows the typing, and showErrors shows every message now, empty fields too. The focus moves on to the expiry and the code only when the part before is complete, and Backspace in an empty field goes back. The fields carry the cc-number, cc-exp, cc-csc and cc-name tokens and numeric keyboards. renderField(part, field) mounts your processor's hosted field for 'number', 'expiry' or 'code' in the same frame (return undefined to keep the built-in one); a part you replace does not count towards valid. showName adds the optional name, now fixes the moment the expiry is checked against, disabled dims the whole frame and turns the fields off (a hosted field is handed disabled to pass on), and labels holds the fixed words.

items.name: card-fieldset-demo
items.title: Card fieldset demo
items.description: A working preview of Card fieldset.

items.name: radio-accordion
items.title: Radio accordion
items.description: Payment or delivery methods as radio rows where the chosen one opens its own panel beneath and the others stay shut.
items.docs: options are { value, label, description?, trailing?, icon?, content?, disabled? }; control the group with value and onValueChange or start it with defaultValue. The group is a radio group, so arrow keys choose and move the focus and Tab leaves it; name it with label (or aria-labelledby). The row is one big target: the label stretches over it and the radio keeps the focus ring. The panel of the chosen row is a region labelled by that row and opens beneath it, the others stay shut, and the focus never moves into a panel by itself. trailing is text at the end of the row ('Free', 'Instant', '4.95'), read out after the description. A closed panel is not in the page: its fields cannot be reached with Tab and a required field in it never blocks a form, so keep what is typed in state of your own, as the demo does. The height animates and is instant under reduced motion.

items.name: radio-accordion-demo
items.title: Radio accordion demo
items.description: A working preview of Radio accordion.

items.name: rating-filter
items.title: Rating filter
items.description: '4 stars and up' as a filter: a radio list of star rows with the number of products beside each and an Any rating choice.
items.docs: value is the lowest rating that passes, or null for any rating; control it with value and onValueChange or start it with defaultValue. options are the ratings to offer, from the highest (4, 3, 2 and 1 by default) and max is how many stars a rating has. counts is { any, 4, 3, 2, 1 }: how many products each choice leaves, cumulative, and optional; without it no counts are shown. It is a radio group, so arrow keys choose and Tab leaves; the stars are decoration and a row is named in words, '4 stars and up, 128 products'. A row whose count is 0 is disabled and reads '0 products'. The chosen row is bold with a check, never only coloured stars, and every row is 44px tall. locale writes the counts and labels holds the fixed words.

items.title: Rating filter demo
items.description: A working preview of Rating filter.

items.name: product-pricing-fieldset
items.title: Product pricing fieldset
items.description: Price, compare-at price and cost for a product form, with the discount, profit and margin worked out as you type.
items.docs: value is { price, compareAt, cost } in minor units (4900 is 49.00), with null for a field that is empty; control it with value and onValueChange or start it with defaultValue. Below the three fields the discount ('20% off', with what it saves), the profit and the margin are worked out in whole minor units and divided once at the end, so nothing is rounded before it is calculated. A fact that cannot be known yet says 'Not enough information', a compare-at price below the price is flagged in words under its field, and a margin below zero is shown plainly with a warning icon and 'Selling below cost'. A screen reader hears the discount, the profit and the margin when a field is left. showCost (true by default) turns the cost field and the profit and margin rows off. currency sets the symbol and the decimals, a comma or a point both work, locale writes the amounts and percentages, and labels holds the fixed words. pricing.ts exports pricingOf(), so your server can check the same numbers.

items.name: product-pricing-fieldset-demo
items.title: Product pricing fieldset demo
items.description: A working preview of Product pricing fieldset.

items.name: stock-adjust-field
items.title: Stock adjust field
items.description: Adjust stock without doing sums: add, remove or set a quantity, give a reason, and see on hand before and after.
items.docs: onHand is the stock now. value is { mode, quantity, reason, note }, with mode 'add', 'remove' or 'set'; control it with value and onValueChange or start it with defaultValue. onValueChange gets the adjustment plus newOnHand (what the stock will be, null while the change is refused) and valid (a usable quantity, a reason, and the note when the reason asks for one), so saving needs no arithmetic, and both follow the number as it is typed (half-typed text such as '2.' waits until the field is left). Each mode keeps its own quantity and Set to starts at what is on hand. The result line always reads 'On hand 24, after 36' in tabular figures and is announced politely; a change that would take the stock below zero is refused with the numbers, unless allowNegative is on. reasons are { value, label, requiresNote? } and default to Received, Sold in store, Damaged, Count correction and Other, where Other makes the note required. unit follows every number, locale writes them and labels holds the fixed words. stock.ts exports stockAfter() and problemsOf() for the same checks on your server.

items.name: stock-adjust-field-demo
items.title: Stock adjust field demo
items.description: A working preview of Stock adjust field.

items.name: category-nav
items.title: Category nav
items.description: A category tree that shows only the current branch: parents above, siblings beside, children below, with counts.
items.docs: tree is the top-level categories as { id, label, href, count?, children? }; currentId says where you are (leave it out at the top, where 'All categories' is the current one). Only that branch is drawn: a link back to all categories, the parents as links, the categories beside the current one (showSiblings), the current one in bold with aria-current='page', and its children indented with counts. More children than maxChildren (6) fold under 'Show N more', and the button stays where it is so the focus is never lost; a fold of a single category is not made. A category with a count of 0 is dimmed, not removed. onNavigate(category, event) runs on a click: call event.preventDefault() to route on the client. linkAs renders the links with your router's Link, allHref is where 'All categories' goes, showCounts turns the counts off, and labels holds the fixed words. It is one nav landmark named Categories and renders on the server.

items.name: category-nav-demo
items.title: Category nav demo
items.description: A working preview of Category nav.

items.name: region-switcher
items.title: Region switcher
items.description: Where you ship to and what you pay in: a country and a currency in one small panel, saved with one button.
items.docs: countries are { code, name, currency, accepts? } and currencies the currencies on offer (the countries' own by default). The trigger reads 'Ship to NL, EUR'; its panel has a searchable list of countries, a currency choice that follows the country but can be changed, and Save. value is the pair that applies now ({ country, currency }); update it in onSave, or start with defaultValue. Nothing applies until Save, and Escape or a click outside closes the panel and drops what was chosen. accepts lists the currencies an order to that country can be paid in besides its own: a currency outside it shows a hint and cannot be saved. note sits above the button (a free shipping threshold, say). open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange control the panel; a panel that starts open does not take the focus, one the visitor opens does. The component never navigates and sets no cookie: what saving means is up to you. locale writes the currency names and labels holds the fixed words.

items.title: Region switcher demo
items.description: A working preview of Region switcher.

items.name: price-breakdown-popover
items.title: Price breakdown popover
items.description: A price you can press to see how it is made up: base, discounts, shipping and VAT as lines that add up to the total, with the rate named.
items.docs: total is what the customer pays, in minor units (4900 is 49.00). lines are { label, amount, kind?, rate?, note? } with kind 'charge' (the default), 'discount' or 'tax'. They render as a real table: a discount shows a minus and the word Discount, a tax shows its rate ('VAT 21%'), and a rule above the total makes the sum readable. Charges add, a discount (passed positive) is taken off, and taxes are added too unless includesTax is on, where they are already in the total and listed under it as 'Includes VAT 21%'. In development a console warning says so when the lines do not add up to the total. Money is formatted in the given currency and locale from whole minor units. The trigger is a button named 'Price breakdown, 49.00 euros' that shows the total with an info icon, or your own trigger; the popover is not modal, so the page stays usable. title, align, open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange work as you would expect (a popover that starts open does not take the focus), and labels holds the fixed words. The trigger has no negative margin, so it never reaches over the word before it; pass className="-ml-1" to line a price up with the text above it. sumOf() in breakdown.ts is the same sum.

items.title: Price breakdown popover demo
items.description: A working preview of Price breakdown popover.

items.name: address-confirm-dialog
items.title: Address confirm dialog
items.description: A checkout dialog for an address that cannot be verified exactly: what was typed beside the suggestion, the differences in bold, to choose from or to edit.
items.docs: entered and suggested are lists of lines, { id, value }, in the order of your form; the id is the field a line comes from ('street', 'postalCode') and lines are matched across the two addresses by id. Within a line the words are compared, so only the words that differ are bold and a screen reader hears 'Changed' before each of them; a line only one address has is bold as a whole. reason says why the address could not be verified, and the sentence under it counts the lines that differ. The suggestion is chosen to begin with (defaultValue, or value with onValueChange). 'Use this address' calls onUseSuggested(suggested), or onKeepEntered(entered) when the typed address is chosen; return a promise and the button shows it is working, the dialog closes when it resolves and stays open when it rejects. 'Edit address' closes the dialog and, once it has closed, calls onEdit with the id of the first line that differs so you can focus that field; the dialog leaves focus to you then (without onEdit, focus goes back to where it was). allowKeep makes the typed address a second choice, 'Keep what I typed', and choosing it opens a warning that delivery may fail; without it the typed address is shown to compare and cannot be chosen. open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange control the dialog and trigger is the element that opens it (without one, focus goes back to where it was). On a short screen the content scrolls and the buttons stay in view. AddressConfirmPanel is the same content without the dialog, for a step in the page. address.ts exports compareAddresses for your own use. Always pass locale; labels holds every word. Nothing is sent anywhere by the component itself.

items.name: address-confirm-dialog-demo
items.title: Address confirm dialog demo
items.description: A working preview of Address confirm dialog.

items.name: offer-list
items.title: Offer list
items.description: Other offers for the same product: seller and rating, condition, delivery and the price with shipping, sortable, with the best price named and an add button per row.
items.docs: offers holds one entry per seller: id, seller, rating and ratingCount, condition ('new', 'like-new', 'very-good', 'good' or 'acceptable'), price and shipping in minor units (shipping 0 is free), delivery as { from, to? } ISO days and an optional note. The cheapest price with shipping is marked 'Best price' in words and with a bar on the row (highlightBest, on by default, needs two offers or more). The list sorts itself by price with shipping, delivery, condition or the seller's rating (the Seller rating column): pass sort and onSort to control it, or defaultSort; offers that tie are put cheapest first, offers without a rating go last, and the change is announced ('Sorted by price, lowest first'). The column heads are real sort buttons with aria-sort. Each condition is a tooltip on the table, reachable from the keyboard; on a device without hover the meaning is written out under the badge instead. Below the container width of 56rem the table becomes cards with a sort control, the condition written out under its badge and the same information. onAdd(offer) may return a promise: the button shows it is working, then 'Added' for a moment, and it is announced; without onAdd there are no buttons. Pass currency, locale and timeZone, so amounts and days read the same on the server and in the browser. A delivery given as a date only ('2026-11-05') is a calendar day and reads the same in every time zone; timeZone places the ones that carry a time of day. labels holds every word, the conditions and their explanations included. sortOffers, totalOf and deliveryText are exported from offers.ts.

items.name: offer-list-demo
items.title: Offer list demo
items.description: A working preview of Offer list.

items.name: line-items-table
items.title: Line items table
items.description: Priced lines as a table: description, quantity, unit price and amount, with subtotal, discount, shipping, VAT and total in a real tfoot, counted in whole cents.
items.docs: lines holds { id, description, detail?, quantity, unit?, unitAmount }, with unitAmount in minor units (8900 is 89.00) and a quantity that may be a fraction (hours, metres). Every amount is worked out in whole minor units and rounded once per row, so the rows always add up to the total: a line is quantity times unitAmount, discount is { label?, percent?, amount? } (the percentage of the subtotal first, then the fixed amount, never more than the subtotal), shipping is an amount or { label, amount } (0 shows 'Free') and taxRate is a percentage (21 for 21%), worked out on the subtotal less the discount plus shipping. The prices exclude VAT unless you set taxIncluded, as on a shop receipt: the row then reads 'Includes VAT 21%' and the total does not change. A row that does not apply is left out, and with nothing to add or take off there is only the total. The footer is a real tfoot with row headers, the total is set apart by a heavier rule and counts to a new value (AnimatedPrice) when the lines, the discount or the shipping change. title names the table; without it labels.caption does. Below the container width of 36rem each line becomes a card with its own subtotal and the footer a description list. It needs no client code of its own, so a Server Component can render it. totalsOf is exported, so your server works out the same figures. Always pass locale; labels holds every word.

items.title: Line items table demo
items.description: A working preview of Line items table.

items.name: price-matrix
items.title: Price matrix
items.description: A price grid for made-to-order products: sizes down, materials or quantities across, every price a radio in one group, the chosen row and column quietly marked.
items.docs: rows and columns are { id, label }; prices is a map by row id and then column id of an amount in minor units (1450 is 14.50), where null or a missing entry means the combination is not offered. Every price that is offered is a radio in one radiogroup named 'A3, 250 g paper, 14.50' (row, column, price), so one choice works with the arrow keys and Space: left and right move along a row, up and down along a column, past combinations that are not offered, and Home and End go to the ends of the row (with Ctrl, of the grid). A combination that is not offered says 'Not available' and cannot be picked. Control the choice with value and onValueChange(value, amount), where value is { row, column } or null, or leave it to defaultValue. The row and the column of the choice are quietly emphasised, markCheapest (on by default) writes 'Lowest price' on the cheapest combination, and the chosen price repeats under the grid in a polite status. The grid shows plain numbers in tabular figures and the currency is said once, in the caption, after your own caption text. Below the container width of 42rem the grid becomes one list per row, with the same radios, and the arrows walk the options in the order they are read. title names the group; without it labels.group does. Always pass locale; labels holds every word, the corner of the grid included.

items.title: Price matrix demo

items.name: metric-strip
items.title: Metric strip
items.description: A joined strip of three to five metrics: label, a figure that eases to new values, the change in an arrow and a word, and an honest dash when data is missing.
items.docs: Pass three to five metrics. `change` is a ratio (0.042 is up 4.2 percent); `null` means there is nothing to compare with, and `value: null` means no data, with `missing` saying why. Keep `format` objects stable so figures ease instead of restarting. While `loading`, pass the metrics you already have and the skeleton draws the same rows, so the strip keeps its height.

items.name: target-pace-card
items.title: Target pace card
items.description: A goal with a deadline: the current value, a bar with a tick where an even pace would be today, the verdict in words and the daily rate still needed.
items.docs: Dates are calendar days in `timeZone`. Pass `now` from the server so the verdict is the same on the server and in the browser. Today counts as half a day, so the answer does not drift while the page is open. Far ahead reads as words ("Well ahead of pace"), never as a four-digit percentage.

items.description: An account balance for fintech and marketplaces: the available and pending split, next payout, actions, a hide toggle and an overdrawn state in words.
items.docs: Figures are in major units. `hidden` is controlled and `defaultHidden` is not; `onToggleHidden` reports the new state. Hidden figures never reach the DOM as text. A date-only `nextPayout.date` ("2026-10-23") is a calendar day and reads the same in every time zone.

items.docs: Pass `now` from the server for a stable first render; without it the card reads the clock in the browser and ticks once a minute. items.title: Greeting header
items.description: A dashboard welcome: a greeting that follows the hour in your time zone, today's date, one sentence from your counts with links, and a primary action.
items.docs: Needs no client code: it renders from props, so it works in a Server Component when the action is a link. Always pass `timeZone` (the user's, not the server's) and, for a stable first render, `now` from the server. A count of zero drops out of the sentence; with none left it says you are all caught up.

items.name: on-call-card
items.title: On-call card
items.description: Who is on call now and next: shift end times in your time zone, a handover flagged in words, an escalation contact and a Page button that asks for a reason.
items.docs: Page asks for a reason first and waits for `onPage` to settle; reject the promise to show the failure and keep the reason. With no `current` shift the card says Nobody is on call and offers to page the escalation contact. Pass `now` for a stable first render.

items.name: facet-filter
items.title: Facet filter
items.description: A filter button that opens a searchable checklist with row counts; picks show on the button as chips or a count, with Clear filter at the foot.
items.docs: Counts are yours to compute: pass how many rows each option would leave given the other filters. Options at zero stay in place, dimmed, so the list never reshuffles while people click. The button's accessible name lists the picks, and on a narrow screen long names in the chips give way with an ellipsis. The list is a multi-select checklist named after the filter, and each option says whether it is checked. Controlled with `value` and `onValueChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultValue`.

items.name: filter-row
items.title: Filter row
items.description: The row of controls above a list: search, your filters and a Reset that counts what is active, folding into one Filters button and a sheet on a phone.
items.docs: Your filters are rendered once and moved between the row and the sheet, so they keep their state, an open panel included. Server rendered, the markup already has the phone's shape at the default 640px (CSS decides until the page is interactive); another `collapseBelow` applies once it is. Reset calls `onReset`, and clearing your filters is yours to do; Done only closes the sheet. Keep the filters controlled so a page reload can restore them. A facet filter's button sizes to its picks, so the controls after it make room when they change.

items.name: dashboard-grid
items.title: Dashboard grid
items.description: A 12-column grid for dashboard widgets: sizes by name, rows of one fixed height so tall and short widgets line up, and one column on a phone.
items.docs: It lays out and nothing else, and it needs no client code. Breakpoints follow the grid's own width (container queries), so it adapts beside a sidebar: twelve columns from 896px, six from 672px, one below. Give every Widget a `label`: each becomes a region. A widget's only child fills it. Row spans apply from the tablet layout up; on a phone a widget is as tall as its content. With `dense` the visual order can differ from the DOM order.

items.name: metric-definition-popover
items.title: Metric definition popover
items.description: Explain a number where it is shown: an info button that opens the metric's definition, formula, source, freshness and owner, so people stop asking what it means.
items.docs: The panel is not in the page until it is opened, so it costs nothing on a table with fifty metrics. Pass `refreshedAt` and, when a source is stale after a different time, `staleAfterHours`. `now` is only for demos and tests. Long names, formulas and table names wrap inside the panel. Focus lands on the panel; Tab then reaches the close button, the copy button and the owner link.

items.name: crosstab-table
items.title: Crosstab table
items.description: One measure by two dimensions with row, column and grand totals, read as a real table and with an optional five-step shading that never hides the number.
items.docs: `totals="row"` adds a Total column (the sum of each row), `"column"` adds a Total row (the sum of each column), `"both"` adds both and the grand total. Cells with no value show a dash and are left out of totals and shading. Give `format` as Intl options to use it from a Server Component. The table sits in a labelled region you can focus, so a sideways scroll works with the keyboard.

items.title: Crosstab table demo

items.name: weighted-scorecard
items.title: Weighted scorecard
items.description: A decision matrix: weighted criteria down the side, options across, a 1 to 5 score in each cell and weighted totals that name the winner or call a tie.
items.docs: Weights can be any positive numbers; they are shown as shares that add up to 100 percent. No option is called the winner until every cell is scored. Controlled with `scores` and `onScoreChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultScores`. `readOnly` shows plain numbers. On a phone the columns shrink so up to four options sit side by side, the winner badge shortens to Top or Tied, and the criterion descriptions stay for screen readers only. Like Crosstab table it sits in a focusable, labelled region so a sideways scroll works with the keyboard.

items.title: Weighted scorecard demo

items.name: raci-matrix
items.title: RACI matrix
items.description: Who does what on a project: tasks down, people across, an R, A, C or I in each cell, and a check that every task has exactly one accountable person.
items.docs: Give it `tasks`, `people` and a `value` map where `value[taskId][personId]` is R, A, C or I. Control it with `value` and `onValueChange` (which also receives what changed), or let it keep its own state from `defaultValue`. It never forces exactly one accountable person: a row with none or with two is flagged in words and counted above the table, and the decision stays yours. Tasks that share a `group` fold under a heading, and a folded group still marks a task that needs attention. From the keyboard, arrow keys move between cells, R, A, C and I set a role, plus and minus step through the roles and Backspace clears one. `readOnly` draws plain letters for an approval screen or a report.

items.name: raci-matrix-demo
items.title: RACI matrix demo
items.description: A working preview of RACI matrix.

items.name: field-diff-table
items.title: Field diff table
items.description: What changed on a record: each field's old and new value side by side, with added and removed values marked in words. For audit trails and approvals.
items.docs: The table is a Server Component, so `formatters` can be plain functions keyed by field name; they are called only for values that are not empty. Only the "Show full text" and "unchanged fields" buttons run in the browser. Leave `kind` out and it follows from `before` and `after`: an empty value (undefined, null, "" or []) reads "was empty" or "removed", while 0 and false are values. Dates are `Date` objects drawn with `locale` and `timeZone`; strings are shown as given. A field name is tidied into a label ("due_date" becomes "Due date"); pass `label` for anything else, such as "SKU".

items.name: field-diff-table-demo
items.title: Field diff table demo
items.description: A working preview of Field diff table.

items.name: data-preview-table
items.title: Data preview table
items.description: A peek at tabular data: row numbers, a type chip on every column, nulls shown as nulls and a clear 'Showing 10 of 12,430 rows'.
items.docs: Rows are arrays in the order of `columns`, or objects keyed by column name. Pass `total` when the data has more rows than you are showing. Numbers are written exactly as they are (no rounding), and a number that arrives as text, as it does from a CSV, keeps every digit and trailing zero ("184.50"). A date without a time ("2026-11-04") stays on that day in every time zone, a day that does not exist ("2026-02-30") is shown as written, and `truncateAt` cuts only text and JSON; a cut value shows in full on hover, on focus and on a tap. Ctrl+C or Cmd+C on a focused cell copies its raw value, so a number is copied without grouping and an object as compact JSON. Giving `onColumnClick` turns the headers into buttons. `maxHeight` makes the rows scroll under a header that stays put.

items.name: data-preview-table-demo
items.title: Data preview table demo
items.description: A working preview of Data preview table.

items.name: virtualized-table
items.title: Virtualized table
items.description: Thousands of rows rendered as a few dozen: a windowed table with a fixed row height, a sticky header and true row counts for screen readers.
items.docs: Every row is the same height (`rowHeight`, default 44) and a cell is one line; longer content is cut with an ellipsis, because a taller row would make the scrollbar lie. Keep rows times rowHeight below about 15 million pixels (a few hundred thousand rows at 44px): browsers cap the height of an element. `aria-rowcount` is the number of rows plus the header, so a screen reader says "row 4,813 of 12,431" for the 4,812th row. Selection plugs in through `getRowProps` (return `data-state="selected"`) and sorting through a column's `sort` and `onSort`, which turn the header into the Table's sort button. Use `getRowKey` when rows are sorted or filtered, `onRangeChange` to load the next page near the end, and a CSS length such as "60vh" for `height`. A column's `cell` is a function, so use the table from a Client Component; columns that only name a key (`id` and a text `header`) also work from a Server Component. Find-in-page cannot see rows that are not rendered.

items.description: The sign-in providers linked to an account: who is connected, as whom and since when, with connect and disconnect per row and a guard on the last way in.

Without canDisconnect, the only connected provider is protected; pass your own rule when a password or passkey also counts as a way in. protectedHint says how to add another way in: a tooltip on the protected provider, and plain text under the row on touch screens and in narrow rows where a tooltip cannot open. items.title: Data export section
items.description: The right of access without a support ticket: pick what to include and a format, request the export, and follow earlier ones by status and expiry.
items.docs: Data in, callbacks out: pass the groups, the earlier exports and onRequest. While an export is preparing (or onRequest is pending) the button rests and the card says it will email the person; add the new export to `exports` with status "preparing" and flip it to "ready" with a size, expiresAt and href when it is done. Dates use the locale and timeZone props (UTC by default); pass `now` to pin the relative "Expires in 5 days". title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.title: Data export section demo

items.name: billing-details-section
items.title: Billing details section
items.description: What appears on invoices: company, address, a tax number checked for format and live, billing emails as chips and a reference, saved as one block.
items.docs: onSave may return a message (shown by the Save button), an object of messages keyed by field (shown against the fields), or nothing. onValidateTaxId resolves true or false for the live "Valid" or "Could not verify"; it runs once the number has the right shape. taxIdLabels adds or changes a country's label, example and pattern over the built-in table in tax-ids.ts. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.name: email-preference-center
items.title: Email preference center
items.description: The page behind 'manage your emails': a frequency per list, a pause for 30 days, and unsubscribe from everything behind one inline confirmation.
items.docs: Works without a signed-in session: pass the address (it is shown partly masked) and save each change from onChange, which may return a promise. A list's frequencies default to Off, Weekly and Monthly. Up to four steps sit side by side (on a phone, long labels become a menu) and more than four are always a menu. The value "off" is what Unsubscribe from everything sets. Leave out onPause, onResume or onUnsubscribeAll to drop that part of the page. Controlled with value, or uncontrolled with defaultValue. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.title: Email preference center demo
items.description: A working preview of Email preference center.

items.name: workspace-profile-section
items.title: Workspace profile section
items.description: A workspace's name, URL, default time zone and language, with a live preview of the address, a warning before links change and a save that lights up.
items.docs: The slug is limited to lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens as you type. onCheckSlug resolves true when an address is free; it is asked after a pause in typing and only for an address that differs from the saved one. Changing the slug shows a warning in words before saving. timeZones takes IANA names, listed in the order you pass them, and languages takes { value, label } pairs; both lists are searchable (a language is also found by its name in `locale`, so "German" finds Deutsch) and have sensible defaults in defaults.ts. While Save runs the fields are locked. Pass the saved workspace back as `workspace` after onSave and the form follows. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.name: workspace-profile-section-demo
items.title: Workspace profile section demo
items.description: A working preview of Workspace profile section.

items.name: branding-settings
items.title: Branding settings
items.description: How a workspace looks to its customers: logos for light and dark, an icon and a brand colour with a contrast check, and live page and email previews.
items.docs: Images are URLs: onUpload receives the chosen file (only SVG and PNG get that far) and resolves to the address it can be shown from, and Save hands back the same four values. An address that turns out not to draw is taken back with a message, so a broken image is never saved. The colour is checked against white and black text (minContrast 4.5 is WCAG AA, 7 is AAA) and against a white page; one that fails is not applied and the reason is shown. colors sets the swatches. The previews are drawn on literal white, because they show the customer's page, not your product. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.name: branding-settings-demo
items.title: Branding settings demo
items.description: A working preview of Branding settings.

items.name: authenticator-setup
items.title: Authenticator setup
items.description: Two-step sign-in setup in one card: scan the QR code or type the key, then confirm with the first six-digit code. It works without a camera.
items.docs: The block draws no QR code: pass your own SVG or image in qr (draw it from the otpauth address with a QR library). It is wrapped with alt text that carries the key, so setup works without a camera, and it sits on a white tile, so keep it dark on light. onVerify resolves true or false; a wrong code is announced and cleared. After success the card shows what you pass as next, usually a button to the recovery codes, and the focus moves to that confirmation so the button is one Tab away. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.name: authenticator-setup-demo
items.title: Authenticator setup demo
items.description: A working preview of Authenticator setup.

items.name: recovery-codes-section
items.title: Recovery codes section
items.description: Recovery codes shown once with copy, download and print, and a checkbox people must tick to confirm they saved them before they can continue.
items.docs: Codes of any length work: they sit two to a row while the longest fits and one to a row when it does not. Pass plain strings for fresh codes, or { code, used } to show which were spent (they are struck through and read Used). With onContinue the block asks for "I have saved these codes" and keeps Continue locked until it is ticked; with onRegenerate a new set is offered behind an inline confirmation, and the new codes come back through `codes`. Print hides everything on the page except a plain sheet of the unused codes. Without onDownload the block saves recovery-codes.txt itself. title, description and headingLevel (2 or 3) rename the heading and set its level.

items.name: recovery-codes-section-demo
items.title: Recovery codes section demo
items.description: A working preview of Recovery codes section.

items.name: transfer-ownership-card
items.title: Transfer ownership card
items.description: Hand a workspace to another member: pick the new owner, read what changes, and confirm by typing the workspace name in a dialog that names what you are giving away.
items.docs: members are the people you would allow as the new owner; a member with disabledReason is listed but cannot be chosen. onTransfer(memberId) may be async: resolve to nothing when it worked, or resolve to (or throw) a message when it failed, and the card keeps the choice and shows it. Leave consequences out for a default list that names the new owner, and confirmDescription out for the default dialog text; say what is true for your product in both. onCancel adds a Cancel button for flows the person can leave.

items.name: transfer-ownership-card-demo
items.title: Transfer ownership card demo
items.description: A working preview of Transfer ownership card.

items.name: early-access-features
items.title: Early access features
items.description: Let people opt into previews: each feature with an Alpha or Beta badge, a switch, what changes and how to undo it, and links to give feedback.
items.docs: Controlled: keep features in state and update enabled in onToggle. Return a promise from onToggle and the switch moves at once and stays busy until it settles; if it rejects, the switch goes back and the row says so. effect and undo are the words shown after a switch is turned on. A feature with disabledReason is locked and says why in text.

items.name: early-access-features-demo
items.title: Early access features demo
items.description: A working preview of Early access features.

items.name: bulk-select-menu
items.title: Bulk select menu
items.description: The header checkbox with a menu for choosing what to select: all, none, unread, starred, with the mixed state and the count in words.
items.docs: Controlled: derive state (none, some or all) from your own selection and keep the selection in your callbacks. The checkbox runs onSelectAll when nothing is selected and onSelectNone otherwise. Each criterion shows the number it would select and is disabled at 0. After every choice a polite message says what was selected.

items.name: bulk-select-menu-demo
items.title: Bulk select menu demo
items.description: A working preview of Bulk select menu.

items.name: copy-as-menu
items.title: Copy as menu
items.description: Copy the same thing in the format the next tool wants: a split button whose menu offers Markdown, JSON, cURL or plain text and remembers the last choice.
items.docs: Each format's serialize() runs only when someone copies in that format, and may return a promise. Pass format and onFormatChange to keep the last choice yourself (in local storage, say), or defaultFormat to leave it to the button. Picking a format in the menu copies in it at once. Set as on a format when it reads badly after Copy as: "plain text" for Plain text. Formats carry functions, so build them in a client component.

items.name: copy-as-menu-demo
items.title: Copy as menu demo
items.description: A working preview of Copy as menu.

items.name: add-to-calendar-button
items.title: Add to calendar button
items.description: Adds an event to the calendar people use, Google, Outlook, Apple or an .ics file, built from one event object with the time zone handled.
items.docs: A start without an offset (2026-11-12T19:00) is read in the event's timeZone; a Date or a string ending in Z or +01:00 is an exact moment. Give end or durationMinutes (default 60). All-day events take a date, and end is the last day. buildIcs, buildGoogleUrl and buildOutlookUrl are pure functions in calendar.ts that return null for an event that cannot be read. Pass uid so an edited event updates the first one in the calendar.

items.name: add-to-calendar-button-demo
items.title: Add to calendar button demo
items.description: A working preview of Add to calendar button.

items.name: directions-button
items.title: Directions button
items.description: Get directions in the maps app people use: Apple Maps on iPhone, Google Maps elsewhere, Waze if they prefer, and the address to copy as a fallback.
items.docs: Give the destination an address (with its name, so the pin is labelled) or latitude and longitude; a name alone is not enough and disables the button with the reason. Without apps, Apple Maps comes first on iPhone and iPad and Google Maps elsewhere, decided after mount. Waze only drives. The link builders in directions.ts are pure and return null for a place that cannot be used.

items.name: directions-button-demo
items.title: Directions button demo
items.description: A working preview of Directions button.

items.name: save-contact-button
items.title: Save contact button
items.description: Save a person or business to the address book: it builds a vCard in the browser from one contact object and downloads it, with no server involved.
items.docs: The file is a vCard 3.0 with escaped text, lines folded at 75 octets and labelled phone, email and address types. On an iPhone it opens the Add Contact sheet. The accessible name adds who it is for, and a contact without a name disables the button with the reason. buildVCard in vcard.ts is pure and returns null without a name, so the same text can become a QR code.

items.name: save-contact-button-demo
items.title: Save contact button demo
items.description: A working preview of Save contact button.

items.name: follow-button
items.title: Follow button
items.description: Follow, Following and Requested in one button: optimistic, with a follower count, a clear way to unfollow and a rollback message when the request fails.
items.docs: Controlled: keep status and count in state and update both in onFollow and onUnfollow before they resolve. The button answers at once and rolls back with a message if the promise rejects; presses are ignored while a request is pending. Resolve onFollow with "requested" when the account needs approval, or pass isPrivate to ask for it up front; unfollowing a private account asks once. defaultStatus leaves the status to the button, and the count then stays as given for that starting status and moves with the button. The error line is wider than the button and widens the control with it, so where you right-align the button pass className="items-end" (or sm:items-end) and it keeps its right edge when a request fails. The accessible name stays "Follow <name>" and aria-pressed carries the state, while the visible word changes to Following or Requested.

items.name: follow-button-demo
items.title: Follow button demo
items.description: A working preview of Follow button.

items.name: like-button
items.title: Like button
items.description: A like button where the count is the point: it answers at once, rolls the number, plays one quiet ring and tells screen readers the exact count.
items.docs: Controlled: keep liked and count in state and update both in onToggle once the request has succeeded; the button already shows the new state while it waits, and rolls back with a message if onToggle rejects. defaultLiked leaves the state to the button, and count then stays as written for that starting state and moves with the button. Counts above 999 abbreviate by locale (1.2K, 1,2 Mio.) while the accessible name and the tooltip keep the exact number. Pass names to make the tooltip read "Liked by ...", and any @rhs-ui/icons glyph as icon: it is drawn filled once liked.

items.name: like-button-demo
items.title: Like button demo
items.description: A working preview of Like button.

items.name: vote-buttons
items.title: Vote buttons
items.description: Up and down arrows around a score for questions, answers and feature requests: one vote each, changeable, with the score announced.
items.docs: Controlled: keep value and score in state and update both in onVote once the request has succeeded. onVote receives "up", "down" or "none" (pressing the chosen arrow again clears the vote). The control moves the score by the right amount while the request is on its way, including two for a switch from down to up, and puts both back with a message in a bubble beside the control (to the right of a vertical one, to the left of a row, whichever side has room) if onVote rejects. score is written for the vote the control starts in. Set subject to name what is voted on, and allowDownvote={false} for a single arrow with a count.

items.name: vote-buttons-demo
items.title: Vote buttons demo
items.description: A working preview of Vote buttons.

items.name: watch-button
items.title: Watch button
items.description: A watch button with levels: all activity, mentions only or nothing, as a split button whose words and bell always say what you will be told.
items.docs: Controlled: keep level and count in state and update both in onLevelChange once the request has succeeded. The main button switches between the last level that was on and "ignore"; the chevron opens a radio menu. Pass levels to change the words (id must stay all, mentions or ignore) and subject for the accessible name ("Watching this issue, all activity"). The count moves by one when watching starts or stops. A rejected onLevelChange rolls everything back with a message.

items.name: watch-button-demo
items.title: Watch button demo
items.description: A working preview of Watch button.

items.name: approval-buttons
items.title: Approval buttons
items.description: Approve and Reject as one decision: a reason when rejecting, who decided and when, and a short window to change your mind.
items.docs: Uncontrolled it runs by itself: Approve and Reject call onApprove and onReject (each may return a promise and shows its own busy and error state), then the status line takes over with Change decision for undoWindow seconds. Controlled, pass status, decidedBy, decidedAt and reason, and set status back to pending in onChangeDecision. Reject always asks for a reason first (requireReason makes it required). Pass locale and timeZone so the time reads the same on the server and in the browser. A decision made here shows just the time on the day it was made and adds the date on any other day; a time you pass in decidedAt always carries its date, so a page rendered on the server reads the same once it has loaded. In a narrow space Change decision drops under the sentence. The control holds no form of its own, so it can sit inside yours, and Ctrl or Cmd with Enter confirms a rejection.

items.name: approval-buttons-demo
items.title: Approval buttons demo
items.description: A working preview of Approval buttons.

items.name: social-sign-in-buttons
items.title: Social sign-in buttons
items.description: Continue-with buttons for sign-in providers: monogram marks instead of brand logos, a last-used tag first in the list, and one busy state.
items.docs: Pass providers (id, label and an optional mark) and onSelect(id). While onSelect runs, that provider's button shows a spinner and the others disable; a rejection puts a message under the list. For a redirect flow pass busy yourself. lastUsed moves a provider first and tags it. The default marks are neutral monogram tiles built from the name (GH for GitHub, G for Google, one letter more when two would match), so no trademarked logo ships; bring your own with mark. In a narrow row the name moves up against its mark so it still fits. layout is stacked, grid or icons (square buttons with a tooltip); the list is labelled for screen readers.

items.name: social-sign-in-buttons-demo
items.title: Social sign-in buttons demo
items.description: A working preview of Social sign-in buttons.

items.name: translate-toggle
items.title: Translate toggle
items.description: Translate a review or comment and back to the original with one quiet control that shows loading, translated-from and failed states.
items.docs: Nothing is translated unless you pass onTranslate(text), which returns the translated string and runs only when the control is pressed; the result is kept, so going back and forth asks once. Uncontrolled it manages its own state. To control it, pass state with onStateChange, and translation once the state is translated. sourceLocale and locale are the language codes that mark each version with lang, so screen readers switch voice. labels changes the words of the control for a site that is not in English.

items.name: translate-toggle-demo
items.title: Translate toggle demo
items.description: A working preview of Translate toggle.

items.name: use-location-button
items.title: Use location button
items.description: A Use my location button that handles every outcome in words: finding you, found with its accuracy, blocked, unavailable and timed out.
items.docs: navigator.geolocation is called only when the button is pressed, never on load. onLocate receives latitude, longitude and accuracy in metres and nothing is sent anywhere; onError receives denied, unavailable or timeout. Where the Permissions API exists, a site that is already blocked says so before the first press. The button renders nothing where there is no geolocation. Pass geolocation to supply your own source (a native shell, or a stub to try every outcome), and labels to change the words.

items.name: use-location-button-demo
items.title: Use location button demo
items.description: A working preview of Use location button.

items.name: keep-awake-toggle
items.title: Keep awake toggle
items.description: A switch that keeps the screen on for recipes, scripts and slides with the Wake Lock API, taking it again after a tab switch.
items.docs: The lock is requested when the switch is turned on, requested again when the tab becomes visible (browsers let go of it while a tab is hidden) and released when it is turned off or the page goes. Nothing is requested on load: a switch that starts on (defaultOn or on) asks for the lock at the first touch or key press. If the browser refuses, the switch returns to off, onChange(false) is called and one line says why. Where the Wake Lock API does not exist the component renders nothing. Pass wakeLock to supply your own source.

items.name: keep-awake-toggle-demo
items.title: Keep awake toggle demo
items.description: A working preview of Keep awake toggle.

items.name: listen-button
items.title: Listen button
items.description: Listen to this article with the browser's own speech: play, pause and stop, a choice of speed, and the sentence being read highlighted.
items.docs: Pass text, or targetRef for an element whose text is read sentence by sentence (the sentence being read is highlighted with the CSS Custom Highlight API, without touching your markup; mark anything that should not be read with data-listen-skip). lang picks the voice and how sentences are cut. The button reads in sentences, which also avoids Chrome stopping long utterances, and stops when the page is hidden or unmounts. Progress is shown as sentences, not time. A page has one voice: pressing a second button stops the first, and if anything else cuts the speech off the button goes back to rest. Where the browser has no speech synthesis it renders nothing; pass engine to supply your own.

items.name: listen-button-demo
items.title: Listen button demo
items.description: A working preview of Listen button.

items.name: reaction-bar
items.title: Reaction bar
items.description: Emoji reactions under a message or comment: counts, your own pressed, who reacted on hover, and an add button with a palette you walk with arrow keys.
items.docs: Keep reactions in state and update it in onToggle (applyReaction does the bookkeeping). The bar shows your press at once; if onToggle rejects it puts the count back and says so in words, and a request in flight blocks a second press on the same emoji. users lists the other people who reacted, so the tooltip can read 'You, Ana Reyes and 2 others'; it may hold only the first few names. max is the most different reactions one message can carry. disabled makes the bar read only: the chips keep full contrast, their tooltip and their place in the tab order (they are aria-disabled, not disabled) and only the add button is dimmed.

items.name: reaction-bar-demo
items.title: Reaction bar demo
items.description: A working preview of Reaction bar.

items.name: inset-sidebar-shell
items.title: Inset sidebar shell
items.description: An app frame with the sidebar on the page background and the page as a bordered, rounded surface beside it, scrolling on its own under a breadcrumb header.
items.docs: Pass your navigation as nav (a SidebarNav is itself the navigation landmark), the account button as footer, and breadcrumbs and actions as header. The page scrolls inside the surface, so the sidebar never moves. Below md the sidebar opens as a left sheet from the menu button and closes when a link is followed. Below lg only the last breadcrumb stays, because the header has no room for a trail that would shrink to a few letters. The first pixels of a scrolled page fade under the header; at rest nothing fades, so padded={false} suits a full-bleed table. The shell is as tall as its container: it is h-dvh unless you pass a height in className. Pass linkAs for your router link and mainId when the page already uses id=main.

items.name: inset-sidebar-shell-demo
items.title: Inset sidebar shell demo
items.description: A working preview of Inset sidebar shell.

items.name: top-nav-shell
items.title: Top navigation shell
items.description: An app frame with the navigation along the top: brand, links with the current one marked, search, actions and account, then the page in a container.
items.docs: Pass links with currentHref (the current link gets aria-current) and your router's Link as linkAs. search, actions and account are slots: from md (or lg, see collapse) they sit in the sticky header, and below that width the links, the search and the actions move into a sheet opened from the menu button while the account stays in the header. pageHeader takes the PageHeader props and is drawn at the top of the content. collapse sets where the row takes over from the menu: md (default) fits four short links next to a labelled action, and five links need collapse="lg" (they want about 820px). With the default, a SearchTrigger shrinks to its icon between md and lg so the row never crowds. The menu closes by itself if the window grows past that width, and the search fills the menu whatever width class it carries. The header gets its bottom border once the page scrolls, measured with an IntersectionObserver. width sets the container to 72rem (default), 80rem or the whole width. Five areas or fewer fit the row; beyond that use a sidebar shell.

items.name: top-nav-shell-demo
items.title: Top navigation shell demo
items.description: A working preview of Top navigation shell.

items.name: settings-shell
items.title: Settings shell
items.description: A settings layout: grouped side navigation, a page title and a focused content column, with the nav becoming a scrolling tab row on phones.
items.docs: Pass groups (labelled lists of links, the SidebarNav shape) with currentHref, plus title, description and actions for the page. backHref adds a Back to app link. The children are the sections of the page: they are stacked with one gap in a column of at most 42rem. From md the navigation sticks under the top of the viewport; on a phone the groups become a row of links that scrolls sideways with faded edges and the current page is scrolled into view. Pass linkAs for your router link.

items.name: settings-shell-demo
items.title: Settings shell demo
items.description: A working preview of Settings shell.

items.name: filter-rail-shell
items.title: Filter rail shell
items.description: A layout for any list narrowed by filters: a rail of filter groups, a results toolbar, removable chips, an announced count and a sheet on phones.
items.docs: filters is a list of groups ({ id, label, activeCount, children }): the shell draws them as collapsible sections, in the rail from lg and in a sheet below it, and never renders both copies at once so no id or label exists twice. chips are the active filters ({ id, label, onRemove }); onClearAll drives Clear all in the row and Clear in the sheet; after Clear in the sheet focus moves to Show N results, so it never leaves the dialog. resultCount is shown, announced politely when it changes (from the page, or from the sheet while it is open, since a modal hides the page from screen readers) and written on the sheet's Show N results button. toolbar holds your sort and view toggle. open and onOpenChange control the sheet if you need to. Keep the filter state in the page, the shell holds none of it.

items.name: filter-rail-shell-demo
items.title: Filter rail shell demo
items.description: A working preview of Filter rail shell.

items.name: wizard-shell
items.title: Wizard shell
items.description: The frame for a multi-step task: a top bar with save and exit, a step rail, the step content and a sticky footer with Back and Continue.
items.docs: Pass steps ({ title, description }), the current index and onContinue; you decide what comes next in your own state. titleAs makes the step heading an h1 (the default, because the step is the page) or an h2. The step's heading takes focus whenever current changes (never on first render), so the new step is announced; finished steps in the rail call onStepChange. Set canContinue to false with canContinueReason and the footer shows that sentence instead of a dead button; on a phone it gets a row of its own above the buttons. onContinue may return a promise: the button shows a spinner until it settles, and errors are yours to handle inside it. onSkip adds Skip for now, onExit adds Save and exit, help is a slot in the header. The last step's button says Finish unless you set continueLabel. The step fades in when it changes (not under reduced motion).

items.name: wizard-shell-demo
items.title: Wizard shell demo
items.description: A working preview of Wizard shell.

items.name: dashboard-shell
items.title: Dashboard shell
items.description: A dashboard frame with named areas: a header with filters, a KPI strip, a main area, a side column and a full-width table zone.
items.docs: Fill the areas you have: kpis, main, side and table are slots, and an empty one leaves no hole (main takes the full width when there is no side). From lg they sit in four columns, below it in reading order. filters is the content of a bar under the title (a period picker, quick filters) that sticks to the top from md up and scrolls away on a phone; updatedAt adds Updated 2 minutes ago, on a row of its own on a phone, written as a full date on the server and turned relative in the browser, with locale and timeZone. Every area is a labelled region; rename them with labels. loading shows a skeleton in each area you filled. Charts are yours: drop them into the slots. Set --sticky-top when a fixed header sits above.

items.name: dashboard-shell-demo
items.title: Dashboard shell demo
items.description: A working preview of Dashboard shell.

items.name: focus-shell
items.title: Focus shell
items.description: A distraction-free frame for one task: a minimal header, a single centred column, a quiet footer and a clear way out.
items.docs: brand sits left in the header and exit (a link back or a close button) right; a ghost Button there is pulled out by its own padding so its text ends on the margin. The column is 24rem (narrow), 32rem (default) or 44rem (wide); align is center or top. footer takes the legal links and language the language switcher. The page is min-h-dvh, never a fixed 100vh: the column is centred with auto margins while there is room and starts at the top when there is not, so the page scrolls normally on a short screen or with the keyboard open. A skip link points at the one main landmark (mainId).

items.name: focus-shell-demo
items.title: Focus shell demo
items.description: A working preview of Focus shell.

items.name: mobile-tab-shell
items.title: Mobile tab shell
items.description: A phone-first app frame: a top bar with title and back, scrolling content and a bottom tab bar that respects the home indicator.
items.docs: Give it a title, three to five tabs ({ id, label, icon, badge }) and the id of the active one. Tabs are real links with aria-current: pass onTabChange to switch screens in state, or leave it out and give each tab an href. The title is large at the top of the content and moves into the app bar once it has scrolled out of view; onBack adds a back button, actions fills the right of the bar, fab floats a round button above the tab bar. The content scrolls on its own with overscroll-contain and ends where the tab bar begins. screenKey (default the active tab) says when the screen has changed: the content then starts at the top and fades in, and the new title takes focus so the change is announced (never on the first render, and not when a tab was pressed, which keeps its focus). The bar clears the notch and the home indicator with env(safe-area-inset-*). From md up the screen is 390px wide and centred; pass a height in className to size it.

items.name: mobile-tab-shell-demo
items.title: Mobile tab shell demo
items.description: A working preview of Mobile tab shell.

items.name: rail-panel-shell
items.title: Rail and panel shell
items.description: A two-level app frame: a slim icon rail for the areas, a panel with the pages of the one you are in, and the content beside them. The panel folds, or opens as a sheet on phones.
items.docs: Pass areas ({ id, label, icon, badge }), the id of the active one and onAreaChange; switch panel (usually a SidebarNav) when the area changes. Each area is a button named for screen readers and in a tooltip, the current one carries aria-current and a filled tile. The panel folds with the toggle at the foot of the rail: panelOpen and onPanelOpenChange control it, or leave them out and the shell keeps it. Below md the panel is a sheet that opens beside the rail when you press an area (pressing another area while it is open switches it in place; an area without a panel opens nothing), closes when you follow a link or press the toggle, and gives focus back to the button you pressed. brand and railFooter fill the top and the foot of the rail, panelActions sits beside the panel's heading. The shell is as tall as its container: it is h-dvh unless you pass a height in className. Pass mainId when the page already uses id=main.

items.name: rail-panel-shell-demo
items.title: Rail and panel shell demo
items.description: A working preview of Rail and panel shell.

items.name: section-sidebar-shell
items.title: Section sidebar shell
items.description: Two-tier navigation: the sections of a product along the top, and a sidebar that lists the pages of the current section only. Sheet and scrolling tabs on phones.
items.docs: Pass sections ({ id, label, href }), the id of the active one, sidebars (the pages of each section in the SidebarNav shape, by section id) and currentHref; the current section is underlined with aria-current, the current page is marked in the sidebar. Pass your router's Link as linkAs: both the sections and the pages use it, so switching section is a normal navigation and focus stays on the link you used. A section without an entry in sidebars has no sidebar. brand and account fill the header; sidebarFooter sits under the sidebar and in the sheet. Below md the sidebar is a left sheet opened from a menu button (focus returns to it, following a link closes it) and the sections scroll sideways under the brand with faded edges.
